morphology_entries.coding_note: Base B-ALL code (CD19 strong + ≥1 of CD10/cCD22/cCD79a, TdT+, MPO−; Dworzak dominant-lineage rule, Pathway §2.3). Upgrade to 9812–9819 only on a documented genetic result. A normal karyotype must not close the branch — ETV6::RUNX1 is cryptic and needs FISH or RT-PCR (§4.4). Landing code for the uncoded B-ALL entities of §5.2 (DUX4-r, ZNF384-r/-like, MEF2D-r, MYC-r, NUTM1-r, TCF3/4::HLF, CDX2/UBTF, PAX5 P80R, PAX5alt, IKZF1 N159Y, iAMP21) — record the genotype in genotype_annotation. KMT2A-r BCP-ALL can drop out of the lineage algorithm (CD10-negative, weak cCD22/cCD79a) and must not default to AML or MPAL. Also the code family for B-ALL in Down syndrome (§4.5), which is a distinct entity from TAM and ML-DS.
morphology_entries.topography_routing_note: Dual-group by compartment. C42.0/C42.1/C42.3/C42.4 (blood/marrow/RES/haematopoietic system NOS) → Group I, Ia1. Otherwise the marrow aspirate decides: more than 25% blasts → Group I, Ia1; 25% or less → Group II, IIb1 (Murphy staging, as printed in Rosolen et al., J Clin Oncol 2015;33:2112, Table 1 footnote). Discriminator is the captured variable `primary_compartment`, asked router-side.

morphology_entries.coding_note: Requires karyotype t(9;22) plus FISH or RT-PCR (record p190 versus p210). Distinguish from CML in lymphoid blast phase: >5% lymphoblasts with BCR::ABL1 and a documented preceding chronic phase is 9875, not 9812 (§3.9).

Low-hypodiploid cases warrant germline TP53 testing — about 50% carry a germline TP53 variant (Li-Fraumeni); record via germline_predisposition (§3.1).

morphology_entries.coding_note: Karyotype plus FISH or RT-PCR. Phenotypic prompt only (not a code substitute): CD9 strong with CD34 negative (§3.1).

morphology_entries.coding_note: Added to the registry code set at ICD-O-3.2 (Pathway §5.7); previously and wrongly advised to 9811. Requires a documented Ph-like signature — CRLF2 rearrangement, an ABL-class fusion or a JAK-STAT lesion — by FISH or RNA-seq; BCR::ABL1 itself must be negative (that is 9812). Enriched in Down-syndrome B-ALL, which is why the trisomy 21 alert is attached (§5.5.1). NOTE: not present in the ICCC-2017 recode table (which predates ICD-O-3.2); Ia1 assignment follows Pathway §1 by analogy with 9811–9818.

morphology_entries.coding_note: Stage 2B morphology-only terminal — lymphoblasts on marrow morphology/cytochemistry with lineage not resolved by flow or IHC. Record why via workup_status (pending / not done / unavailable / declined). Upgrade to 9811 or 9837 once lineage markers are available (§2.5).

cCD3 or sCD3 positive plus CD7 positive with cMPO negative or weak (all three required, Dworzak). Landing code for ETP-ALL, near-ETP and BCL11B-rearranged ETP — none has an ICD-O-3 code (§3.2, §5.2); record the Chandra 5-marker score and phenotype in genotype_annotation. Boundary with T/myeloid MPAL (9809) is MPO: MPO-positive by the Bras rule (≥20% of blasts above the lymphocyte-derived threshold) is 9809, MPO-negative is 9837 (§4.2).
morphology_entries.topography_routing_note: Dual-group by compartment. C42.0/C42.1/C42.3/C42.4 (blood/marrow/RES/haematopoietic system NOS) → Group I, Ia1 (T-ALL). C42.2 (spleen) and every nodal or extranodal site (C00.0–C41.9, C44.0–C77.9) → Group II, IIb1 Precursor cell lymphomas, i.e. T-lymphoblastic lymphoma. Otherwise the marrow aspirate decides: more than 25% blasts → Group I; 25% or less → Group II (Murphy staging, as printed in Rosolen et al., J Clin Oncol 2015;33:2112, Table 1 footnote). Discriminator is the captured variable `primary_compartment`, asked router-side. Confirmed against Layer 1 ICCC-2017, which lists 9811–9818 and 9837 under both Ia1 and IIb1 by topography.

morphology_entries.morphology_name: B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma
morphology_entries.coding_note: Requires ≥5×10⁹/L clonal B cells sustained ≥3 months plus the ERIC/ESCCA core panel (CD19, CD5, CD20, CD23, kappa, lambda); borderline cases add CD43, CD79b, CD81, CD200, CD10, ROR1 (§3.11). Adult-only entity — retained in the code set per §7.5, do not remove.
morphology_entries.topography_routing_note: Dual-group by compartment. C42.0/C42.1/C42.3/C42.4 → Group I, Ia2 (CLL). C42.2 (spleen) and every nodal/extranodal site → Group II, IIb2 (SLL). Discriminator is the captured variable `primary_compartment`, asked router-side.

morphology_entries.coding_note: Kept live as the lineage-indeterminate fallback (Pathway §5.3.5); ICD-O-3.2 lists it Preferred/current. Prefer 9833 (B-cell type) or 9834 (T-cell type) whenever lineage is determinable — 9832 is for the genuinely indeterminate residual only. Diagnosis of exclusion: rule out CLL transformation, mantle cell lymphoma and splenic marginal zone lymphoma.
Diagnosis of exclusion (ICC) — rule out CLL transformation, mantle cell lymphoma and splenic marginal zone lymphoma before coding (§3.11). Adult-only entity — retained per §7.5, do not remove.

CD11c/CD25/CD103/CD123 positive with annexin-A1; BRAF V600E confirmatory. HCL-variant and splenic B-cell lymphoma/leukaemia with prominent nucleoli are BRAF V600E negative, have no dedicated code and fall to 9940 with a variant flag (§5.2) — the variant status does not change the code. Adult-only entity — retained per §7.5, do not remove.

morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Mature T-cell and NK cell leukemias
morphology_entries.coding_note: HTLV-1 serology is mandatory and code-defining — an unconfirmed mature T-cell leukaemia goes to 9820, never to 9827 (§3.11, §6). Serology is recorded under Molecular/PCR in this schema's closed test vocabulary. Shimoyama subtypes (acute / lymphomatous / chronic / smouldering) are code-neutral — all remain 9827. Adult-only in practice (decades of latency).
morphology_entries.topography_routing_note: Dual-group by compartment. Leukaemic phase (C42.0/C42.1/C42.3/C42.4) → Group I, Ia3. Lymphomatous phase, nodal or extranodal → Group II, IIb3. Shimoyama subtype is recorded as annotation and does not change the code.

morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Mature T-cell and NK cell leukemias
morphology_entries.coding_note: CD3+CD8+CD57+ with a clonal TCR rearrangement; STAT3/STAT5B mutation supportive. Threshold ≥0.5×10⁹/L sustained (§3.11). Do not use 9831 for NK-lineage LGL disease — indolent NK-LGLL has no dedicated code and 9948 is an aggressive-disease code (§5.3.3).

morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Mature T-cell and NK cell leukemias
morphology_entries.coding_note: Major criteria: >5×10⁹/L cells with a T-PLL phenotype, demonstrated T-cell clonality, and 14q32/Xq28 abnormality or TCL1/MTCP1 involvement — inv(14) or t(14;14) on karyotype/FISH (§3.11). Adult-only entity — retained per §7.5, do not remove.

morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Mature T-cell and NK cell leukemias
morphology_entries.coding_note: CD3− CD16+ CD56+ with EBV positivity. Occurs in adolescents and young adults — genuinely relevant paediatrically. Registry policy: indolent NK-LGLL codes to 9948 unchanged with no indolent flag; survival analysis is done separately in biostatistics, not derived from the morphology code (§5.3.3). NK-LGLL diagnostic rule (Pastoret): ≥3 major criteria, or ≥2 major plus 2 minor. Two major criteria with no histological investigation is an explicitly unresolved grey zone — carry as a non-terminal state, do not force the call (§3.11). STAT3/STAT5B/CCL22/TET2 mutations are code-neutral.

Valid Ia4 terminal for a blood/marrow-presenting case with no further characterisation (Pathway §5.5.4). Dual-group by topography and confirmed as such by registry policy (§5.3.10) — see topography_routing_note. Prefer 9820 when the process is explicitly leukaemic; 9591 is for a non-Hodgkin lymphoma NOS abstracted at a Group I topography.
morphology_entries.topography_routing_note: Dual-group by topography (Pathway §5.3.10). C42.0/C42.1/C42.3/C42.4 (blood/marrow/RES/haematopoietic system NOS) → Group I, Ia4. C42.2 (spleen) and every other site → Group II, IIb4 (Non-Hodgkin lymphomas, NOS).

morphology_entries.coding_note: Chain-termination root for the lymphoid fallback chains (Pathway §7.4) — nos_fallback_code is null by design. Reachable from a referral note alone. Also the mandated landing code for an unconfirmed mature T-cell leukaemia (never default to 9827 without confirmed HTLV-1 positivity, §6). Record why the case is NOS via workup_status.

Legacy FAB frame (≥80% erythroid, ≥30% proerythroblasts). ICD-O-3.2 code retained, but the blast denominator is now all nucleated marrow cells rather than non-erythroid cells, which retires the old erythroid/myeloid AEL split — 9840 no longer matches any current WHO definition (§2.2). Code conservatively to 9861 if uncertain.

Base AML code — MPO positive by the Bras rule (≥20% of blasts above the lymphocyte-derived threshold) or ≥2 of CD13/CD33/CD64/CD65/CD117 with B- and T-lineage criteria not met. Retained deliberately: WHO-HAEM5 eliminates 'AML, NOS' but ICC retains it and the registry code list requires it (§5.4). Landing code for the uncoded AML entities of §5.2 — NUP98-r, KAT6A::CREBBP, TP53-mutated AML — record the genotype in genotype_annotation. Also the resolution code for a myeloid sarcoma with concurrent marrow AML when the AML is unsubtyped (one case, coded as the AML — §4.7, §5.3.8).

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Acute myeloid leukemia with t(6;9)(p23;q34); DEK-NUP214
morphology_entries.coding_note: Karyotype plus FISH for t(6;9) DEK::NUP214.

HAEMATOLOGICAL EMERGENCY. Presumptive treatment (hypergranular promyelocytes/faggot cells plus coagulopathy → immediate ATRA) is a treatment rule, not a coding rule. For coding, confirm by FISH, RT-PCR/RQ-PCR/RT-QLAMP or anti-PML immunostaining; run RT-PCR in parallel where available (defines the PML::RARA isoform and enables MRD). Treat anti-PML IF as lower confidence unless the reader is experienced. Flow signature: HLA-DR−, CD34−, CD117 heterogeneous, MPO bright, CD15 dim/absent, CD13 heterogeneous, CD33 bright, high side scatter; microgranular variant (M3v) has lower SSC, frequent CD2/CD34 and high WBC but is still 9866. Mimic: an APL-like phenotype with CD4 positive, low/moderate SSC and high WBC — do not code 9866 until PML::RARA is molecularly excluded; if negative and NPM1-mutated, code 9877 (§3.6). PML::RARA isoform is code-neutral.
Use only if the report explicitly states the subtype (granulocytic plus monocytic differentiation). No dedicated corpus evidence — code conservatively to 9861 otherwise.

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Acute myeloid leukemia with inv(3)(q21;q26.2) or t(3;3)(q21;q26.2); RPN1-EVI1
morphology_entries.coding_note: Karyotype plus FISH for inv(3)(q21q26.2) or t(3;3)(q21;q26.2). Current nomenclature is GATA2::MECOM; the REDCap option string retains the older RPN1-EVI1 label and contains a transcription error in the translocation notation ('t(13.3)') — copied verbatim as required, flagged to the registry for correction.

Defined in classification anchors only, no dedicated corpus evidence. Use only if the report explicitly states acute basophilic leukaemia; otherwise 9861. Note that basophilic lineage is one of the five lineages that must be actively excluded before a positive AUL diagnosis (9801) — no basophilic marker is sourced in the evidence base (§4.1).

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Acute myeloid leukemia with abnormal marrow eosinophils
morphology_entries.coding_note: Karyotype plus FISH for inv(16)(p13.1q22) / t(16;16); CBFB::MYH11. The REDCap option string uses the descriptive morphological label ('with abnormal marrow eosinophils') rather than the genetic label — same code, copied verbatim as required.

Distinguished from acute undifferentiated leukaemia (9801/AUL) in the ALAL literature: 9872 still meets a myeloid lineage-defining criterion, AUL does not (§4.1). Requires a comprehensive panel to make the distinction safely.
FAB-descriptive terminal, no dedicated corpus evidence. Use only if the report explicitly states the subtype; otherwise 9861.
FAB-descriptive terminal, no dedicated corpus evidence. Use only if the report explicitly states the subtype; otherwise 9861.

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Acute myeloid leukemia with mutated NPM1
morphology_entries.coding_note: Added to the registry code set at ICD-O-3.2 (Pathway §5.7); previously and wrongly advised to 9861. Requires a documented NPM1 mutation. Principal APL mimic: shares CD33+/CD13+/cMPO+ with CD34−/HLA-DR− but is CD4-positive with low-to-moderate side scatter and high WBC, where APL has high SSC. Code 9877 only once PML::RARA is molecularly excluded (§3.6). Registry applies the ICC ≥10% blast floor (§5.4). NOTE: not present in the ICCC-2017 recode table (which predates ICD-O-3.2); Ib assignment follows Pathway §1.

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Acute myeloid leukemia with biallelic mutation of CEBPA
morphology_entries.coding_note: Added to the registry code set at ICD-O-3.2 (Pathway §5.7); previously and wrongly advised to 9861. Requires biallelic CEBPA mutation, or an in-frame bZIP mutation. One of the two blast-threshold exceptions: WHO-HAEM5 exempts both BCR::ABL1 and CEBPA from the blast requirement, ICC/ELN exempt only BCR::ABL1 from the ≥10% rule. The registry applies ICC thresholds (§5.4), so ≥10% blasts is required here. NOTE: not present in the ICCC-2017 recode table (which predates ICD-O-3.2); Ib assignment follows Pathway §1.

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Acute myeloid leukemia with mutated RUNX1
morphology_entries.coding_note: Added to the registry code set at ICD-O-3.2 (Pathway §5.7); previously and wrongly advised to 9895. Requires a documented RUNX1 mutation. Boundary with 9895: RUNX1 is also a member of the nine-gene MDS-related set, so a case with a RUNX1 mutation and MDS-related cytogenetics or other MDS-related gene mutations may resolve to 9895 instead — record which rule was applied in classification_system. TP53-mutated (VAF ≥10%) takes precedence over both (§3.7). NOTE: not present in the ICCC-2017 recode table (which predates ICD-O-3.2); Ib assignment follows Pathway §1.

Use only if the report explicitly states the subtype. Monocytic differentiation is established by ≥2 of non-specific esterase, CD11c, CD14, CD64, lysozyme (§2.3). No dedicated corpus evidence for the code itself — code conservatively to 9861 otherwise.

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Acute myeloid leukemia with myelodysplasia-related changes
morphology_entries.coding_note: Requires MDS-related cytogenetics or a mutation in the nine-gene set (ASXL1, BCOR, EZH2, RUNX1, SF3B1, SRSF2, STAG2, U2AF1, ZRSR2), irrespective of prior MDS history (ELN 2022). TP53-mutated at VAF ≥10% takes precedence as a separate entity. WHO-HAEM5 treats AML-MR as a single entity; ICC splits it into TP53-mutated / MDS-related-gene / MDS-related-cytogenetic — record which was applied in classification_system (§3.7, §5.4). Exclusion rule: AML-MR-defining genetics or a complex karyotype exclude MPAL, so a biphenotypic immunophenotype with these genetics codes 9895, not 9805–9809 (§4.1).

Karyotype plus FISH for t(8;21)(q22;q22); RUNX1::RUNX1T1. Trap: aberrant CD19, PAX5 and cCD79a co-expression is common and is easily misread as B-lineage or MPAL. Aberrant B-marker expression in an MPO-strong blast population with t(8;21) is 9896 (§4.3).
KMT2A break-apart FISH. Myeloid lineage must be established first — a KMT2A rearrangement with B-lineage criteria is 9813, and with both B/T and myeloid criteria met is 9807 (§4.1).

TRANSIENT ABNORMAL MYELOPOIESIS (TAM) — behaviour /1, the non-malignant member of the behaviour-overloaded 9898 pair. Criteria: age <3 months, confirmed trisomy 21, GATA1s mutation, spontaneous resolution. NON-REPORTABLE as a malignancy (§4.5, §4.9) — this entry exists so the behaviour code can be recorded, not so a malignant registration can be raised. Never code 9898/3 for a TAM case. NOTE — UNRESOLVED, REFERRED TO THE REGISTRAR: §4.9 assigns TAM to 9898/1 while the §5.6 alert (reproduced verbatim in clinical_alert) says 'never code 9898' without qualifying the behaviour. §3.8 states 'TAM → 9898/1 … Never 9898/3', which reads as the /3 behaviour being the thing prohibited. This entry is authored on that reading — the /1 behaviour is recordable, non-reportable as a malignancy — but the alert text is left unnarrowed and the question is referred to the registrar for a ruling before go-live. Needs a watch flag with a re-entry path: 10–20% progress to true ML-DS, which is then coded 9898/3 at that later diagnosis. nos_fallback_code is deliberately null — a non-reportable terminal must never be wired to a malignant NOS fallback (§7.5). Distinguish from the third trisomy 21 entity, B-ALL in Down syndrome (9811 family, frequently CRLF2-rearranged). No REDCap dropdown option exists for the /1 behaviour — the single 9898 option string names the /3 entity only.

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Myeloid leukemia associated with Down syndrome
morphology_entries.coding_note: MYELOID LEUKAEMIA OF DOWN SYNDROME (ML-DS) — behaviour /3, the malignant member of the behaviour-overloaded 9898 pair. Criteria: age ≥3 months, confirmed trisomy 21, GATA1s mutation, blast criteria met (§3.8). Below 3 months with spontaneous resolution the case is TAM (9898/1) and is non-reportable. A TAM that later progresses re-enters here. Distinguish from the third trisomy 21 entity, B-ALL in Down syndrome (9811 family, frequently CRLF2-rearranged) — §4.5.

Flow pitfall: platelet adherence gives false-positive surface CD41/CD61 — wash adequately; intracellular CD61 is more specific. Landing code for the uncoded AMKL fusions of §5.2 — CBFA2T3::GLIS2 (cryptic on karyotype, needs RT-PCR/NGS; trisomy 3; 'RAM phenotype' = bright CD56, dim CD45/CD38, HLA-DR negative), NUP98-r AMKL and KMT2A-r AMKL — record the genotype in genotype_annotation. A normal karyotype must not close the CBFA2T3::GLIS2 branch (§4.4). t(1;22) upgrades to 9911.

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Acute myeloid leukemia (megakaryoblastic) with t(1;22)(p13;q13); RBM15-MKL1
morphology_entries.coding_note: Karyotype plus FISH for t(1;22)(p13;q13). Current nomenclature is RBM15::MRTFA; the REDCap option string retains the older RBM15-MKL1 label — same code, copied verbatim as required (§3.8).

Added to the registry code set at ICD-O-3.2 (Pathway §5.7); previously and wrongly advised to 9861. Requires BCR::ABL1 plus AML criteria. Must be distinguished from CML in myeloid blast phase, which is 9875 — ask whether a preceding chronic phase is documented (§1, §3.9). BCR::ABL1 is the one abnormality for which both WHO-HAEM5 and ICC retain a blast-count requirement (§3.7, §5.4). NOTE: not present in the ICCC-2017 recode table (which predates ICD-O-3.2); Ib assignment follows Pathway §1.

CLOSED AS A TERMINAL (Pathway §4.8, §5.3.7). ELN 2022 holds that therapy-related myeloid neoplasm is no longer a disease entity — prior cytotoxic therapy is a QUALIFIER on the underlying diagnosis. Retained in the code set so historical records resolve, but no tree may land on it: terminal_reachable is false. Instead, code the underlying entity (for example, therapy-related AML with MDS-related cytogenetics resolves to 9895), capture prior_cytotoxic_therapy at document_inventory and set qualifiers: [therapy_related] on the output block. Build lint: prior_cytotoxic_therapy = yes together with a resolved code of 9920 or 9987 is a build error.

The one Group I code that is not C42.x — coded to the involved site's topography (orbit, skin, lymph node, bone, testis, GI tract, peritoneum) via a site_resolution node (§4.7). primary_sites is deliberately left open. IHC markers are listed in order of frequency; about 30% are MPO-negative — the 'chloroma' green colour is MPO-driven but its absence does not exclude the diagnosis. Isolated myeloid sarcoma with a negative marrow is still 9930. Concurrent marrow AML is ONE case coded as the AML (SEER Rule M3, registry policy §5.3.8) — resolve to the specific AML subtype, or 9861 if unsubtyped, record the extramedullary site in topography and set myeloid_sarcoma_present. Misclassification risk: orbital or cutaneous myeloid sarcoma is easily mistaken for a Group II lymphoma or a Group IX soft-tissue sarcoma.
morphology_entries.topography_routing_note: **Always Group I (Ib), regardless of presenting site.** An orbital, cutaneous, nodal or other extramedullary myeloid sarcoma must **not** be re-routed to Group II or IX. Record the involved site in topography; it does not change the group. `primary_sites` is deliberately left open — 9930 is the one Group I code that is not C42.x.

morphology_entries.coding_note: Defined in classification anchors only, no dedicated corpus evidence. Requires a trephine (marrow fibrosis with panmyeloid proliferation). Use only if the report explicitly states it; otherwise 9861.

PLACEHOLDER ONLY — 'BCR::ABL1 pending'. Never a positive diagnosis (§3.9). Once BCR::ABL1 is confirmed positive the code is 9875 regardless of phase; if BCR::ABL1 is confirmed negative, reassess against atypical CML (9876) and the other MPN entities, not 9863. Record karyotype_result_status so a true NOS is distinguishable from an incomplete workup.

Karyotype t(9;22) plus RT-PCR, with FISH optional. BCR::ABL1 positive is 9875 REGARDLESS OF PHASE — phase is staging annotation, never a separate code (§3.9). Registry phase definition: WHO 2022 (chronic <20% blasts, blast phase ≥20%, no accelerated tier); record cml_phase for display only, never in resolution logic. Lymphoid blast crisis can masquerade as ALL: >5% morphologically apparent lymphoblasts with BCR::ABL1 and a documented preceding chronic phase is 9875, not 9812. Advanced phases can be present at diagnosis and must be distinguished from progression on TKI therapy. Transcript isoform (p190/p210) is code-neutral. There is no valid downgrade to a lesser CML code — the cytogenetics node's fallback is 9960 (§7.4).

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Atypical chronic myeloid leukemia, BCR/ABL negative
morphology_entries.coding_note: WBC ≥13×10⁹/L with immature granulocytes ≥10% of WBC, PB/BM blasts <20%, dysgranulopoiesis (hypo/hypersegmented neutrophils, abnormal chromatin clumping), eosinophils <10%, monocytes <10%, hypercellular marrow with granulocytic hyperplasia and dysplasia. Excludes BCR::ABL1 and the myeloid/lymphoid-neoplasm-with-eosinophilia kinase fusions. ICC additionally requires an MDS-qualifying cytopenia. SETBP1/ETNK1 are supportive, not required. Basophils <2% distinguishes it from CML but is not itself a formal criterion. WHO-HAEM5 renames this 'MDS/MPN with neutrophilia'; ICC keeps 'atypical CML' — naming only, same code (§3.9, §5.4).
Hb >16.5 g/dL (male) or >16.0 g/dL (female), or Hct >49% (male) or >48% (female), plus a JAK2 mutation. Vanishingly rare in children — confirm independently and flag for senior review.

Chain-termination root for the chronic myeloproliferative and eosinophilic fallback chains (Pathway §7.4) — nos_fallback_code is null by design. Also the mandated fallback for the CML cytogenetics node, which has no valid downgrade to a lesser CML code. Record why the case is NOS via workup_status and karyotype_result_status.
Trephine required: megakaryocyte atypia plus a graded reticulin stain, with a driver mutation (JAK2, CALR or MPL). Vanishingly rare in children — confirm independently and flag for senior review.
Platelets ≥450×10⁹/L with a JAK2, CALR or MPL mutation. Vanishingly rare in children — confirm independently and flag for senior review.

The gate is a DISJUNCTION and the registry adopts both routes (§3.9, §5.4). Route A (WHO-HAEM5, and ICC when CSF3R-negative): WBC ≥25×10⁹/L, molecular not required. Route B (ICC only): WBC ≥13×10⁹/L with an activating CSF3R mutation. Shared criteria for either route: segmented plus banded neutrophils ≥80% of WBC, precursors <10% of WBC, no significant dysgranulopoiesis, monocytes <10% of leukocytes, circulating blasts rare, hypercellular marrow with increased neutrophils showing normal maturation, and exclusion of BCR::ABL1-positive CML, PV, ET, PMF and myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and kinase fusions. ICC non-molecular alternative where CSF3R is unavailable: persistent neutrophilia ≥3 months plus splenomegaly plus documented exclusion of reactive causes. Phase is not a code: 10–19% blasts is accelerated phase, ≥20% is blast phase. Record classification_system.

STEP 1 IS A HARD GATE, not optional: exclude and document secondary causes first — parasitic (strongyloides, schistosoma, filariasis, hookworm, toxocara), HIV, drugs, allergy, autoimmune and solid-tumour-associated. In the UCI catchment hypereosinophilia is overwhelmingly parasitic or HIV-related; skipping step 1 is the largest single false-positive registration risk in Group I (§3.10). Only then test FIP1L1::PDGFRA (→ 9965), then karyotype for 5q31-33 PDGFRB (→ 9966) and 8p11-12 FGFR1 (→ 9967), then PCM1::JAK2 (→ 9968). 9964 is the terminal when clonality is demonstrated but no specific fusion is identified, and the provisional landing code for ETV6::ABL1 and FLT3-fusion cases, which have no dedicated ICD-O-3 code (§5.2) — record the fusion in genotype_annotation. No clonality demonstrated is idiopathic HES: NON-REPORTABLE, not 9964. Registry applies ICC criteria for CEL versus HES (§5.4).

morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Myelodysplastic syndrome and other myeloproliferative diseases
morphology_entries.coding_note: Persistent monocytosis, both absolute (≥0.5×10⁹/L) AND relative (≥10% of WBC), with blasts <20%. CMML-1 is PB <5% / BM <10% blasts; CMML-2 is 5–19% / 10–19%. Two-tier supporting-criteria rule: monocytosis ≥1×10⁹/L requires ≥1 supporting criterion; monocytosis 0.5–<1×10⁹/L requires BOTH (dysplasia ≥10% in ≥1 lineage; clonal cytogenetic or molecular evidence). Exclude reactive monocytosis, especially at the ≥1×10⁹/L level (TB and other infection are common in the UCI catchment). CMUS/CCMUS — persistent monocytosis ≥10% and ≥0.5×10⁹/L with the criteria not met — is NOT malignant, has no code and must not be reported (§3.10, §4.9). WHO-HAEM5 and ICC have converged on the monocyte threshold, so no arbitration applies.

morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Myelodysplastic syndrome and other myeloproliferative diseases
morphology_entries.coding_note: Category I (clinical/haematological, all four assessed, last two MANDATORY): PB monocytes ≥1×10⁹/L (absent in about 7%); splenomegaly (absent in about 3%); blasts <20% in PB and BM (mandatory); absence of BCR::ABL1 (mandatory). Category II (genetic, ≥1 required, present in >95% of true JMML): somatic PTPN11, KRAS, NRAS or RRAS; germline NF1 with LOH, or clinical NF1 (≥6 café-au-lait macules >5 mm); germline CBL with LOH. Supporting: HbF elevated for age, circulating myeloid precursors, monosomy 7. AGE IS NOT DIAGNOSTIC — prognostic only. Noonan-spectrum myeloproliferative disease (germline PTPN11/KRAS/NRAS/RIT1 with NO somatic secondary mutation, normal karyotype, self-limiting) is a distinct non-reportable entity — do not auto-code 9946. ICC's RAS-negative 'JMML-like neoplasm' category is NOT adopted; those cases code to 9975 on their own merits (§3.4, §5.3.2). DNA-methylation subgroups (LM/IM/HM) are prognostic and code-neutral. Spontaneous regression (about 15%) does not retract the diagnosis — code at diagnosis on the evidence then available (§5.3.9). Also exclude malaria/HIV hypersplenism, which confounds the splenomegaly and monocyte criteria (§4.9).

morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Myelodysplastic syndrome and other myeloproliferative diseases
morphology_entries.coding_note: MDS/MPN overlap not meeting the criteria for CMML, atypical CML, JMML or MDS/MPN-RS-T. Also the landing code for RAS-pathway-negative JMML-like mimics, including ALK, ROS1, FIP1L1::RARA and CCDC88C::FLT3 fusions — ICC's 'JMML-like neoplasm' category is not adopted, and these cases are coded 9975 on their own merits, not 9946 (§3.4, §5.2, §5.3.2). Record the fusion in genotype_annotation. Chain-termination root for the MDS/MPN fallback chain (Pathway §7.4) — nos_fallback_code is null by design. Note the REDCap option string ends with a full stop; it is reproduced verbatim.

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Myelodysplastic syndrome with single lineage dysplasia
morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Myelodysplastic syndrome and other myeloproliferative diseases
morphology_entries.coding_note: FAB-era term, retained as a live code. Also the ICD-O-3.2 replacement for the retired 9991 (refractory neutropenia) and 9992 (refractory thrombocytopenia) — §5.7. Not a paediatric entity in practice: the working paediatric MDS code set is 9985 (RCC / low blast), 9983 (excess blasts) and 9989 (NOS). SEER over-counting rule: within the MDS family code only the first subtype diagnosed; do not re-abstract a later, more specific MDS subtype (§3.5).

morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Myelodysplastic syndrome and other myeloproliferative diseases
morphology_entries.coding_note: Ring sideroblasts (iron stain on the marrow aspirate) with an SF3B1 mutation. Note the REDCap option string reads 'Refractory anemia with sideroblasts' whereas Pathway §1 names the entity 'Refractory anemia with ring sideroblasts' — the REDCap string is reproduced verbatim as required. Under 1% of paediatric MDS; adult-only in practice — retained per §7.5, do not remove. SEER over-counting rule applies (§3.5).

morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Myelodysplastic syndrome and other myeloproliferative diseases
morphology_entries.coding_note: Paediatric MDS with excess blasts: BM blasts 5–19%, PB blasts 2–19% — the paediatric band, which the registry applies because ICC explicitly excludes patients under 18 years from the 'MDS/AML' 10–19% category (§2.2, §5.4). Part of the working paediatric MDS code set with 9985 and 9989. Mandatory pre-conditions before any sporadic paediatric MDS code: germline predisposition screen (GATA2, SAMD9/SAMD9L, RUNX1, ANKRD26, ETV6), IBMFS exclusion (chromosome breakage/G2 arrest for Fanconi, telomere length for dyskeratosis congenita, consider Shwachman-Diamond), and — Uganda addition — exclusion of nutritional (B12/folate/iron) and HIV-related cytopenia first (§3.5). SEER over-counting rule applies.

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Refractory anemia with excess blasts in transformation
morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Myelodysplastic syndrome and other myeloproliferative diseases
morphology_entries.coding_note: OBSOLETE — abolished in 2001. WHO 2001 lowered the AML blast threshold from 30% to 20%, absorbing the whole RAEB-T band; the code has had no live entity behind it since (Pathway §5.3.6). Retained only so pre-2001 archival records and aliases resolve; must never be selected as a live terminal and must never be the nos_fallback_code of another entry. A current case in the old RAEB-T blast band is an AML — code the AML entity.

morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Myelodysplastic syndrome and other myeloproliferative diseases
morphology_entries.coding_note: THE PAEDIATRIC RCC CODE — the commonest MDS of childhood (about 50%). SEER lists 'Refractory cytopenia of childhood (RCC)' and 'Childhood MDS with low blasts (cMDS-LB)' as explicit alternate names for 9985/3; the current WHO-5 label is 'MDS with low blasts, NOS'. This is a code-currency fact, not a registry decision, and requires no sign-off (§3.5, §5.3.1). Criteria (ICC): persistent age-adjusted cytopenia; dysplasia in ≥2 lineages or ≥10% in one; blasts PB <2% and BM <5%; no prior cytotoxic therapy; no fibrosis. About 80% have a hypocellular marrow with patchy erythroid islands; monosomy 7 in about 20%. CD61 or CD41 IHC ON THE TREPHINE IS MANDATORY — it identifies micromegakaryocytes, the feature that separates RCC from severe aplastic anaemia, the key differential and a non-reportable terminal. Mandatory pre-conditions as for 9983 (germline screen, IBMFS exclusion, nutritional and HIV exclusion) — germline findings are recorded as a modifier and do not change the code. SEER over-counting rule applies.

morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Myelodysplastic syndrome and other myeloproliferative diseases
morphology_entries.coding_note: Isolated del(5q) on karyotype or FISH. Rare in children; adult-only in practice — retained per §7.5, do not remove. SEER over-counting rule applies (§3.5).

morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Myelodysplastic syndrome and other myeloproliferative diseases
morphology_entries.coding_note: CLOSED AS A TERMINAL (Pathway §4.8, §5.3.7) — same handling as 9920. Prior cytotoxic therapy is a QUALIFIER on the underlying diagnosis (ELN 2022), not a separate entity. Retained in the code set so historical records resolve, but no tree may land on it: terminal_reachable is false. Code the underlying MDS subtype, capture prior_cytotoxic_therapy at document_inventory and set qualifiers: [therapy_related] on the output block. Build lint: prior_cytotoxic_therapy = yes together with a resolved code of 9920 or 9987 is a build error.

morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Myelodysplastic syndrome and other myeloproliferative diseases
morphology_entries.coding_note: Chain-termination root for the MDS fallback chain (Pathway §7.4) — nos_fallback_code is null by design. Use when dysplasia is documented but the subtype is not stated. Part of the working paediatric MDS code set with 9985 and 9983. Record why the case is NOS via workup_status. SEER over-counting rule: code only the first MDS subtype diagnosed; do not re-abstract a later, more specific subtype (§3.5).

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Myelodysplastic syndrome with ring sideroblasts and multilineage dysplasia
morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Myelodysplastic syndrome and other myeloproliferative diseases
morphology_entries.coding_note: Added to the registry code set at ICD-O-3.2 (Pathway §5.7); not addressed by the previous 76-code list. Ring sideroblasts plus multilineage dysplasia, with or without an SF3B1 mutation. Adult-predominant — keep the age-implausibility warning; rare in children. Distinguish from 9982 (ring sideroblasts, single lineage). SEER over-counting rule applies (§3.5). NOTE: not present in the ICCC-2017 recode table (which predates ICD-O-3.2); Id assignment follows Pathway §1.

Root chain-termination code for the whole group (Pathway §7.4) — nos_fallback_code is null by design. Stage 2A clinical-alias terminal for a referral note that says only 'leukaemia' with no lineage and no acuity. LOW confidence by definition. Record why via workup_status (pending / not done / unavailable / declined); 'cytogenetics unavailable at UCI' is a legitimate, permanent terminal state (§2.5). Upgrade to 9801, 9820 or 9860 as soon as acuity or lineage is documented.

THREE SITUATIONS ON ONE CODE, disambiguated by workup_status plus alal_subtype (§4.1). (1) AUL — a POSITIVE diagnosis of exclusion: comprehensive panel, no lineage-defining marker (MPO, CD3, and the B-lineage set) and no more than ONE lineage-associated marker for ANY single lineage; workup_status complete, alal_subtype aul. (2) ALAL-NOS — ≥2 markers of one lineage but no lineage-defining marker; workup_status complete, alal_subtype alal_nos. 9805 is wrong for ALAL-NOS by definition (9805 is MPAL-NOS, which ALAL-NOS explicitly does not meet). (3) NOS sense — lineage not established because the panel was incomplete, unavailable, not done or declined; alal_subtype null; do not report as AUL. The workup_status values pending / not done / unavailable / declined must be reachable only by the third row. Panel adequacy is the second gate: five lineages must be actively excluded — megakaryocytic (CD41/CD61 negative), erythrocytic (glycophorin A negative), NK (CD56 negative) as hard gates; plasmacytoid dendritic (CD123/HLA-DR/CD11c negative) as a SOFT warning only, since CD123 alone does not settle it and CD303/BDCA-2, TCL1 and TCF4 are better but unsourced; and basophilic, for which no marker is sourced. Cases assignable to another genetically or clinically defined category (AML-MR, AML with a defining genetic abnormality, therapy-related AML, CML blast crisis, myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with a kinase fusion) are NOT AUL — code that entity. Check for BCL11B rearrangement/activation before coding 9801. 'Acute leukemia, NOS' is ICD-O-3.2's own preferred term; the AUL preferred term is a WHO 2008 change already inside ICD-O-3 before 3.2 (§5.7).

MPAL-NOS — MPAL criteria met but the combination is neither B/myeloid nor T/myeloid, or the combination is unspecified. Requires total blasts ≥20%. NOT AUL: acute undifferentiated leukaemia is 9801 with alal_subtype aul (§4.1). Lineage criteria per §2.3 (WHO-HAEM5), applied GENETICS-FIRST — evaluate BCR::ABL1 and KMT2A before falling through to the unconditioned rules. Two exclusion rules WHO 2016 lacked: AML-MR-defining genetics or a complex karyotype code 9895, not MPAL; a divergent-lineage clone in <5% of cells codes the dominant leukaemia with a descriptive modifier, not MPAL. Do not use the AIEOP-BFM 'dominant lineage' treatment-track label as the diagnosis.

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Mixed phenotype acute leukemia with t(9;22)(q34;q11.2); BCR-ABL1
morphology_entries.nos_fallback_name: Mixed phenotype acute leukemia, B/myeloid, NOS
morphology_entries.coding_note: B plus myeloid lineage criteria met with BCR::ABL1 positive. Not evidenced as a named subtype in the corpus — resolve it from the lineage criteria (§2.3) plus the genetic result, not from a report label. Molecular 'when' conditions must precede unconditioned rules in the resolution logic (§7.3 #3, §7.5 ordering lint).

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Mixed phenotype acute leukemia with t(v;11q23); MLL rearranged
morphology_entries.coding_note: B or T plus myeloid lineage criteria met with a KMT2A rearrangement. Fallback is 9805 rather than 9808/9809 because this code does not itself fix the lymphoid lineage. Not evidenced as a named subtype in the corpus — resolve it from the lineage criteria plus KMT2A break-apart FISH, not from a report label. Molecular 'when' conditions must precede unconditioned rules in the resolution logic (§7.3 #3, §7.5 ordering lint).

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Mixed phenotype acute leukemia, B/myeloid, NOS
morphology_entries.coding_note: B AND myeloid criteria both met with no defining genetics (§4.1). B criterion: CD19 strong plus ≥1 strongly expressed of CD10/CD22/CD79a, or CD19 weak plus ≥2 of the same; CD79a is only valid if T lineage is not under consideration. Myeloid criterion: MPO above the Bras threshold on the SAME blast population, or monocytic differentiation by ≥2 of non-specific esterase, CD11c, CD14, CD64, lysozyme. Landing code for MPAL-ZNF384-r (about 50% of paediatric B/myeloid MPAL), which has no ICD-O-3 code — record the genotype in genotype_annotation (§5.2).

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Mixed phenotype acute leukemia, T/myeloid, NOS
morphology_entries.coding_note: T AND myeloid criteria both met with no defining genetics (§4.1). T criterion: cytoplasmic or surface CD3 with intensity in part exceeding 50% of the mature T-cell level (anti-CD3 epsilon-chain antibody), or immunocytochemistry positive with a non-zeta-chain reagent. Boundary with ETP-ALL (9837) is MPO: MPO-positive by the Bras rule is 9809, MPO-negative is 9837 — getting this wrong moves the case between the two codes (§4.2). Landing code for ALAL-BCL11B-r (about 20–30% of T/myeloid MPAL and of ETP-ALL), which has no ICD-O-3 code — record the genotype in genotype_annotation (§5.2).

Chain-termination root for the myeloid fallback chain (Pathway §7.4) — nos_fallback_code is null by design. Reachable from a referral note that establishes myeloid lineage but neither acuity nor subtype. Record why via workup_status.

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Myeloid or lymphoid neoplasm with PDGFRA rearrangement
morphology_entries.coding_note: CRYPTIC — FIP1L1::PDGFRA is invisible on karyotype; requires FISH for the CHIC2 deletion or RT-PCR. A normal karyotype must never close this branch or resolve to 9964 (§4.4, §7.5). The secondary-eosinophilia exclusion cascade (parasitic, HIV, drugs, allergy, autoimmune, solid-tumour-associated) is a hard gate that must be documented BEFORE this code is reachable (§3.10). Clinically important because these cases are imatinib-responsive.
Karyotype 5q31-33 rearrangement confirmed by FISH. The secondary-eosinophilia exclusion cascade is a hard gate that must be documented before this code is reachable (§3.10).

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Myeloid or lymphoid neoplasm with FGFR1 abnormalities
morphology_entries.coding_note: Karyotype 8p11-12 abnormality confirmed by FISH. The secondary-eosinophilia exclusion cascade is a hard gate that must be documented before this code is reachable (§3.10).

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Myeloid or lymphoid neoplasm with PCM1-JAK2
morphology_entries.coding_note: Added to the registry code set at ICD-O-3.2 (Pathway §5.7); previously and wrongly advised to 9964. Requires t(8;9)(p22;p24) on karyotype, or FISH, or RT-PCR for PCM1::JAK2. The secondary-eosinophilia exclusion cascade is a hard gate that must be documented before this code is reachable (§3.10). NOTE: not present in the ICCC-2017 recode table (which predates ICD-O-3.2); Ie assignment follows Pathway §1.

nodes.question: What tests are in this patient's file?
nodes.hint: This is the evidence gate. It fixes what precision is achievable and drives every 'upgrade available' line on the output block.
nodes.coding_note: Group I has no imaging-sufficient route — imaging is staging only (Pathway §0).

options.label: Referral / clinical note only — no marrow report
Marrow aspirate, blood film or trephine morphology only — no flow cytometry, no IHC
Marrow aspirate or blood film and a genetic test — no flow cytometry, no IHC
Trephine biopsy and a genetic test — no flow cytometry, no IHC
Morphology and flow cytometry
Morphology and IHC, no flow cytometry
Trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) confirmed or suspected — neonatal or infant blasts
options.coding_note: Three entities share trisomy 21 and must be separated before coding: TAM, ML-DS and B-ALL in Down syndrome (Pathway §4.5).

options.label: Extramedullary mass with a myeloid phenotype (myeloid sarcoma / chloroma)
Malignancy excluded on review — reactive, non-neoplastic or the diagnosis was revised
options.reason: The abstractor recorded that this case is not a reportable malignancy. No morphology code is emitted and the case leaves the malignant registry.

nodes.question: What exactly does the referral or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: A bare 'leukaemia' must not be coded as acute leukaemia — the wording chooses the code.
nodes.coding_note: Referral-only tier: confidence is LOW and every downstream test is listed as an upgrade. Record why the case is NOS via workup_status.

options.label: Note reads "acute leukaemia", "blast crisis" or "acute blast picture" — lineage not stated
options.upgrade_path: Marrow morphology would give a lineage-level code (9835 or 9861); flow cytometry would give a lineage-specific code.
options.coding_note: 9801 in its NOS sense — lineage not established. Do not report this as a positive AUL diagnosis (Pathway §4.1).

options.label: Note reads "acute myeloid leukaemia" / "AML" with no marrow report in the file
options.upgrade_path: Marrow morphology would support 9861; flow cytometry and cytogenetics would subtype it.

options.label: Note reads only "leukaemia" — acuity not stated
options.upgrade_path: Marrow morphology and a blast count would establish acuity and lineage.
options.coding_note: Acuity is not stated, so 9801 (acute leukaemia) would over-code the referral. 9800 is the honest code.

nodes.question: What does the marrow aspirate / blood film report describe?
nodes.hint: Cytochemistry (MPO, Sudan black, PAS, non-specific esterase) counts as morphology, not as flow cytometry.
nodes.coding_note: Morphology-only tier: lineage-level codes, confidence MEDIUM. Flow cytometry is the upgrade.

options.label: Lymphoid blasts — MPO / Sudan black negative on cytochemistry
options.upgrade_path: Flow cytometry (CD19/CD10/TdT vs cCD3/CD7) would separate B-ALL (9811) from T-ALL (9837). If a BCR::ABL1 result is on file, flow cytometry or IHC (to settle B or T lineage) and any history of a chronic phase are needed before 9812 (B-ALL), 9806 (mixed phenotype) or 9875 (chronic myeloid leukaemia in lymphoid blast phase).

options.label: Myeloid blasts — Auer rods and/or MPO / Sudan black positive cytochemistry
options.upgrade_path: Flow cytometry and cytogenetics/FISH would subtype the AML (9865–9912). If a BCR::ABL1 result is on file, the blast count and any history of a chronic phase are needed before 9912 (AML with BCR::ABL1) or 9875 (chronic myeloid leukaemia in blast phase).

options.label: Hypergranular promyelocytes / faggot cells with coagulopathy (DIC)
options.coding_note: Presumptive APL is a treatment rule, not a coding rule (Pathway §3.6). PML::RARA must be confirmed before 9866 is emitted.

options.label: Blasts present but lineage not stated in the report
options.upgrade_path: Flow cytometry would establish lineage. Cytogenetics/FISH would subtype it.
options.coding_note: 9801 in its NOS sense — lineage not established, workup incomplete. Not a positive AUL diagnosis.

options.label: Marrow reviewed — no leukaemic population; reactive or non-neoplastic
options.reason: Marrow morphology showed no leukaemic population. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.

nodes.question: What does the blood film, marrow aspirate or trephine report describe?
nodes.hint: Cytochemistry (MPO, Sudan black, PAS, non-specific esterase) counts as morphology, not as flow cytometry.
nodes.coding_note: Asked before the lineage markers when the file holds a marrow, film or trephine report with flow cytometry or IHC (registrar, 14 Oct 2026). If no marker rule on ac_lineage_assignment fires, the case reverts to the answer given here and takes the closest diagnosis. No option writes evidence_tests, so the tick-derived evidence is kept.

options.label: Lymphoid blasts — MPO / Sudan black negative on cytochemistry
options.coding_note: Closest diagnosis 9835 if no marker defines a lineage. Held as morphology_finding and read only by the last rules of ac_lineage_assignment: a marker combination that defines a lineage overrides it.

options.label: Myeloid blasts — Auer rods and/or MPO / Sudan black positive cytochemistry
options.coding_note: Closest diagnosis 9861 if no marker defines a lineage. Held as morphology_finding and read only by the last rules of ac_lineage_assignment: a marker combination that defines a lineage overrides it.

options.label: Hypergranular promyelocytes / faggot cells with coagulopathy (DIC)
options.coding_note: Presumptive APL is a treatment rule, not a coding rule (Pathway §3.6). If no marker defines a lineage the case goes to the lineage-route PML::RARA question. Held as morphology_finding and read only by the last rules of ac_lineage_assignment: a marker combination that defines a lineage overrides it.

options.label: Two distinct blast populations, or the report states "mixed phenotype" / "biphenotypic acute leukaemia"
options.coding_note: Closest diagnosis 9805 if the markers entered do not meet the lineage criteria. Replaces ac_alal_resolve option 4. Held as morphology_finding and read only by the last rules of ac_lineage_assignment: a marker combination that defines a lineage overrides it.

options.label: Blasts present, lineage not stated in the report
options.coding_note: Closest diagnosis 9801 if no marker defines a lineage. Held as morphology_finding and read only by the last rules of ac_lineage_assignment: a marker combination that defines a lineage overrides it.

options.label: Marrow reviewed — no leukaemic population; reactive or non-neoplastic
options.reason: Morphology showed no leukaemic population. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.

nodes.question: Is there a cytogenetics / FISH / molecular report, and what does it show?
nodes.hint: Genetics are evaluated BEFORE lineage (Pathway §4.1) — they override the blast threshold and they decide the MPAL fork.
nodes.coding_note: Only AML-BCR::ABL1 and AML-CEBPA still require a blast threshold; the rest of the defining set overrides it (WHO-HAEM5). ICC applies a ≥10% floor to the same list instead of removing it.

options.label: No cytogenetics / FISH / molecular report in the file
Genetics report in the file: no defining abnormality found (for example BCR::ABL1 negative)
Karyotype normal, and no FISH or RT-PCR in the file
options.coding_note: A normal karyotype closes nothing. The cryptic set (ETV6::RUNX1, CBFA2T3::GLIS2, FIP1L1::PDGFRA, masked hypodiploidy) is invisible on karyotype.

options.label: BCR::ABL1 positive: t(9;22) on karyotype, or positive on FISH or RT-PCR
options.coding_note: BCR::ABL1 does NOT override the blast threshold — AML-BCR::ABL1 still requires ≥20% (WHO-HAEM5) / ≥10% (ICC). Lineage assignment decides between 9812, 9806 and 9912.

Trisomy 21 confirmed — GATA1s not tested
options.coding_note: GATA1s is the molecular anchor of both TAM and ML-DS. Without it the TAM/ML-DS distinction rests on age and course alone.

options.label: Trisomy 21 confirmed — GATA1s NEGATIVE
options.coding_note: GATA1s negative is neither TAM nor ML-DS. Assign lineage normally — B-ALL in Down syndrome is the commonest alternative.

options.label: Down syndrome suspected clinically — constitutional karyotype not done
Trisomy 21 EXCLUDED — neonatal myeloproliferation, transient and resolving, no defining genetics
options.reason: Neonatal myeloproliferative disease without Down syndrome, transient and resolving. Treated as provisional / watch, not coded (Pathway §4.6). Re-enter the tool if the disease persists or progresses.

options.label: Trisomy 21 EXCLUDED — persistent disease meeting acute leukaemia criteria

nodes.question: Age at diagnosis, in completed months?
nodes.hint: Three months is the dividing line between transient abnormal myelopoiesis and myeloid leukaemia of Down syndrome.
nodes.coding_note: 9898 is behaviour-overloaded: 9898/1 is TAM (non-reportable) and 9898/3 is ML-DS. The behaviour, not the four-digit code, carries the distinction.

override_when.coding_note: Trisomy 21 excluded — neither TAM nor ML-DS applies. Assign lineage normally.
GATA1s negative — neither TAM nor ML-DS. B-ALL in Down syndrome (9811 family, frequently CRLF2-rearranged) is a separate real entity and is coded on its own lineage evidence.

GATA1s not tested. Myeloid leukaemia of Down syndrome needs a positive GATA1s result (Pathway §1, §3.8), so 9898/3 cannot be emitted on age alone. Assign lineage normally; B-ALL in Down syndrome is a separate entity (Pathway §4.5).

bands.coding_note: Under three months with GATA1s — confirm the TAM triad before anything is coded.
Myeloid leukaemia of Down syndrome — 9898/3. Confirm the blast criteria are met; ML-DS is a malignant, reportable diagnosis.
Age not documented — the TAM/ML-DS distinction must be resolved explicitly before a code is emitted. Do not default to the malignant code.

nos_fallback.name: Acute myeloid leukemia, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Down syndrome context recorded but the TAM/ML-DS distinction could not be resolved.

nodes.question: Confirm the transient abnormal myelopoiesis triad and the clinical course.
nodes.hint: TAM resolves spontaneously. 10–20% later progress to true ML-DS — the watch flag matters.
nodes.coding_note: TAM is ICD-O 9898/1 and is NOT a reportable malignancy. This branch must never emit 9898/3. Spontaneous regression does not retract a diagnosis that was malignant at the time — but TAM was never malignant to begin with (Pathway §3.4, §4.9).

options.label: TAM criteria met — trisomy 21, GATA1s positive, age under 3 months, resolving course
options.reason: Transient abnormal myelopoiesis (ICD-O 9898/1) is not a reportable malignancy. No morphology code is emitted. Set the watch flag: 10–20% of cases progress to myeloid leukaemia of Down syndrome — re-enter the tool if blasts persist or recur at or after three months.

options.label: Blasts have persisted or recurred at or after 3 months — progression to ML-DS
options.coding_note: Progression from TAM to ML-DS. Code 9898/3 at the date the ML-DS criteria were first met.

options.label: Course not documented, or the triad is incomplete
options.reason: The TAM/ML-DS distinction is unresolved in a Down syndrome infant. Treated as provisional / watch and not coded as a malignancy. Re-enter the tool once the course is documented or the GATA1s and blast criteria are available.

nodes.question: Which extramedullary site does the myeloid sarcoma involve?
nodes.hint: IHC order of frequency: CD68-KP1 > MPO > CD117 > CD99 > CD68/PG-M1 > lysozyme > CD34 > TdT > CD56. Around 30% are MPO-negative — its absence does not exclude the diagnosis.
nodes.coding_note: 9930 is the one Group I code that is not C42.x. The site goes into topography; it never changes the group. An isolated myeloid sarcoma with a negative marrow is still 9930, managed as systemic AML.

options.coding_note: Orbital myeloid sarcoma is easily mistaken for a Group II lymphoma or a Group IX soft-tissue sarcoma. It is Group I (Ib).
Cutaneous myeloid sarcoma is easily mistaken for a Group IX soft-tissue sarcoma. It is Group I (Ib).
Nodal myeloid sarcoma must not be re-routed to Group II.

options.site: Concurrent marrow AML at diagnosis (or diagnosed shortly apart)
options.coding_note: SEER Rule M3 — an extramedullary sarcoma and marrow leukaemia of the same lineage are ONE primary. Code the AML entity (specific subtype, or 9861 if unsubtyped), not 9930. Record the extramedullary site and set myeloid_sarcoma_present.

decision_trees.tree_label: Mature B-cell, T-cell and NK-cell leukaemias and the lymphoid NOS codes

nodes.question: What tests are in this patient's file?
nodes.hint: This is the evidence gate. It fixes what precision is achievable and drives every 'upgrade available' line on the output block.
nodes.coding_note: This tree owns the mature lymphoid leukaemias: Ia2 (9823, 9832, 9833, 9940), Ia3 (9827, 9831, 9834, 9948) and the Ia4 NOS codes (9820, 9591). Group I has no imaging-sufficient route — imaging is staging only (Pathway §0). Precursor (blast) disease belongs to the acute tree; leukaemic Burkitt is no longer a Group I code at all and is referred to Group II (Pathway §3.3, §5.3.11).

options.label: Referral / clinical note only — no blood film, no marrow, no flow report
Blood film, marrow aspirate or trephine morphology only — no flow cytometry, no IHC
Morphology and flow cytometry
Morphology and IHC, no flow cytometry
The marrow shows 20% or more blasts — an acute leukaemia, not a mature lymphoid neoplasm
options.coding_note: Cross-tree handover (Pathway §7.1). Blasts at or above 20% are acute leukaemia and the acute tree owns Ia1 and Ib. The mature lymphoid tree emits no precursor code.

options.label: Malignancy excluded on review — reactive lymphocytosis, viral, or the diagnosis was revised
options.reason: The abstractor recorded that this case is not a reportable malignancy. No morphology code is emitted and the case leaves the malignant registry.

nodes.question: What exactly does the referral or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: A referral naming an entity is not a flow report. At this tier the wording chooses a placeholder code, not a diagnosis.
nodes.coding_note: Referral-only tier: confidence is LOW and every downstream test is listed as an upgrade. 9820 is the chain-termination root for the lymphoid fallback chains (Pathway §6, §7.4) and the mandated landing code for an unconfirmed mature T-cell leukaemia. Record why the case is NOS via workup_status.

options.label: Note reads "CLL", "chronic lymphocytic leukaemia", "SLL" or "small lymphocytic lymphoma" — no flow report in the file
options.upgrade_path: Flow cytometry with the ERIC/ESCCA core panel (CD19, CD5, CD20, CD23, kappa, lambda) plus an absolute clonal B-cell count would resolve 9823.
options.coding_note: A referral word is not a flow result. 9823 requires at least 5×10⁹/L clonal B cells with the core panel (Pathway §3.11); the wording alone cannot support it, and CLL is an adult-only entity that must be independently confirmed in a child. 9820 is the honest code.

options.label: Note reads "hairy cell leukaemia" or "HCL" — no flow, no IHC
options.upgrade_path: CD11c, CD25, CD103, CD123 and annexin-A1, plus BRAF V600E, would resolve 9940.
options.coding_note: 9940 is defined by its marker panel (Pathway §3.11). An adult-only entity named in a referral note is not evidence of it.

options.label: Note reads "ATL", "ATLL" or "HTLV-1 associated leukaemia/lymphoma" — no serology result in the file
options.upgrade_path: Confirmed HTLV-1 serology (screening EIA confirmed by western blot / line immunoassay, or proviral DNA) with a mature CD4+ phenotype would resolve 9827.
options.coding_note: Do not default to 9827 without confirmed HTLV-1 positivity (Pathway §6). The referral word is not the serology.

options.label: Note reads "prolymphocytic leukaemia", "B-PLL" or "T-PLL" — no flow report
options.upgrade_path: Flow lineage markers (CD19/CD20 versus CD3/CD5/CD7 and TCL1) would resolve 9833, 9834 or 9832.
options.coding_note: 9832 is kept live as the lineage-indeterminate fallback (Pathway §5.3.5), but it still requires a flow report establishing a prolymphocytic leukaemia. A referral word supports neither it nor 9833/9834.

options.label: Note reads "NK-cell leukaemia", "LGL leukaemia" or "large granular lymphocytic leukaemia" — no flow report
options.upgrade_path: Flow (CD3, CD8, CD57, CD16, CD56, CD94/NKG2A), TCR clonality and a STAT3/STAT5B panel would resolve 9831 or 9948.
options.coding_note: T-LGL (9831) and aggressive NK-cell leukaemia (9948) are separate codes with separate criteria; the referral wording rarely distinguishes them.

options.label: Note reads "non-Hodgkin lymphoma" or "NHL" with no subtype stated
options.coding_note: 9591 is dual-group by topography (Pathway §5.3.10). The site decides Group I (Ia4) or Group II (IIb4), so it must be settled before the code is emitted.

options.label: Note reads "lymphocytosis" or "lymphocytic leukaemia" with no further detail
options.upgrade_path: A blood film with an absolute lymphocyte count, and flow cytometry, would establish lineage and entity.
options.coding_note: Lineage is stated (lymphoid) but no entity is. 9820 is the correct NOS parent (Pathway §6).

options.label: Note reads only "leukaemia" — neither lineage nor acuity stated
options.upgrade_path: A blood film and a blast count would establish acuity and lineage.
options.coding_note: Root chain-termination code for the whole group (Pathway §6, §7.4). 9820 asserts a lymphoid lineage the note does not state.

nodes.question: What does the blood film, marrow aspirate or trephine report describe?
nodes.hint: Cytochemistry and a manual differential count as morphology, not as flow cytometry.
nodes.coding_note: Morphology-only tier: NOS-parent and placeholder codes, confidence MEDIUM at best. Flow cytometry is the upgrade for every branch here — none of the Ia2/Ia3 entities is diagnosable on morphology alone.

options.label: Absolute lymphocytosis of small mature lymphocytes with smudge (Gumprecht) cells — no flow
options.upgrade_path: The ERIC/ESCCA core panel (CD19, CD5, CD20, CD23, kappa, lambda) plus an absolute clonal B-cell count would resolve 9823.
options.coding_note: Morphology cannot separate CLL from a reactive lymphocytosis, from monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis, or from mantle-cell / marginal-zone disease in leukaemic phase. 9823 requires the panel (Pathway §3.11). 9820 is the honest code; it requires only a referral-tier record, which this case exceeds.

options.label: Prolymphocytes (large nucleolated cells) over 55% of the lymphoid population — no flow
options.upgrade_path: Flow lineage markers (CD19/CD20 versus CD3/CD5/CD7, and TCL1) would resolve 9833 or 9834. Cytogenetics for inv(14)/t(14;14) would confirm T-PLL.
options.coding_note: 9832 (PLL, NOS) is kept live precisely for the lineage-indeterminate residual (Pathway §5.3.5) — a morphological prolymphocytic picture with no immunophenotype is exactly that. Prefer 9833 (B-cell) or 9834 (T-cell) as soon as lineage is determinable.

options.label: Lymphoid cells with circumferential hairy cytoplasmic projections; dry tap or reticulin-fibrotic marrow — no flow, no IHC
options.upgrade_path: CD11c, CD25, CD103, CD123 and annexin-A1 by flow or IHC, plus BRAF V600E, would resolve 9940.
options.coding_note: Hairy morphology is suggestive, not diagnostic — splenic marginal zone lymphoma with villous lymphocytes is the main mimic and is a Group II entity. 9940 requires the marker panel (Pathway §3.11).

options.label: Large granular lymphocytes with azurophilic granules — no flow
options.upgrade_path: Flow (CD3, CD8, CD57, CD16, CD56, CD94/NKG2A) with an absolute LGL count, TCR clonality and a STAT3/STAT5B panel would resolve 9831 or 9948.
options.coding_note: Large granular lymphocytes are a normal blood constituent and expand reactively. Neither 9831 nor 9948 is codeable without lineage and clonality (Pathway §3.11).

options.label: Pleomorphic lymphoid cells with multilobated "flower" nuclei, with or without hypercalcaemia — no flow, no serology
options.upgrade_path: Confirmed HTLV-1 serology plus a mature CD4+CD25+ phenotype would resolve 9827.
options.coding_note: Flower cells are suggestive of ATLL but HTLV-1 serology is mandatory and code-defining. 9827 is structurally unreachable from this tier (Pathway §6).

options.label: Medium-sized cells with deeply basophilic vacuolated cytoplasm, starry-sky pattern (FAB L3) — Burkitt suspected
options.coding_note: Burkitt is no longer a Group I code. Leukaemic Burkitt codes 9687/3 in Group II (IIc) from 1 January 2021; 9826 is retired (Pathway §3.3, §5.3.11, §5.7c).

options.label: Marrow or tissue reported as "non-Hodgkin lymphoma, NOS" with no subtype stated
options.coding_note: 9591 is dual-group by topography (Pathway §5.3.10, §5.5.4). The site decides Group I (Ia4) or Group II (IIb4).

options.label: Blasts 20% or more of nucleated marrow cells — an acute leukaemia
options.coding_note: Cross-tree handover (Pathway §7.1). The acute tree's blast gate re-reads the percentage and owns every precursor code.

options.label: Film reviewed — the lymphocytosis is reactive (viral, EBV, pertussis, HIV, post-splenectomy)
options.reason: A reactive lymphocytosis is not a lymphoid neoplasm. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9 principle). Re-enter if a clonal population is later demonstrated.

nodes.question: Where is the disease? Settle this before any code is chosen.
nodes.hint: The router asks this once as its dual-group discriminator; this node confirms it against the report in front of you.
nodes.coding_note: 9823 (CLL/SLL) and 9827 (ATLL) sit in Group I or Group II by COMPARTMENT, not by morphology (DT master §6; Pathway §5.1, §5.3). C42.0/C42.1/C42.3/C42.4 → Group I. C42.2 (spleen), nodal and extranodal → Group II. A nodal-only case is not a Group I leukaemia and must be referred, not coded here.

options.label: Blood and/or bone marrow — a leukaemic presentation (C42.0 / C42.1 / C42.3 / C42.4)
Marrow involvement together with nodal disease — the marrow is the dominant compartment
options.coding_note: Marrow-dominant disease routes to Group I on the compartment discriminator even when nodes are involved.

options.label: Lymph nodes only — no blood or marrow involvement
options.reason: Nodal-only disease with no blood or marrow involvement is a Group II lymphoma, not a Group I leukaemia. If the immunophenotype shows CD5+CD23+ clonal B cells the entity is small lymphocytic lymphoma and still codes 9823, but in Group II (IIb2); any other subtype is resolved by the Group II tree. No Group I code is emitted (DT master §6; Pathway §5.3).

options.label: Spleen only (C42.2) — splenomegaly with no blood or marrow involvement
options.reason: C42.2 (spleen) is deliberately carved out of the Group I topography set for the lymphoid dual-group codes. A splenic presentation routes to Group II. No Group I code is emitted (Pathway §1 Ia4, §5.3.10).

options.label: Extranodal tissue only (skin, gut, CNS, other) — no blood or marrow involvement
options.reason: Extranodal disease with no blood or marrow involvement is a Group II lymphoma. No Group I code is emitted (DT master §6).

options.label: Compartment not stated in the file
options.coding_note: The compartment is left unset rather than guessed. The topography captured at Stage 1 then decides the group for the dual-group codes; an undocumented compartment must be recorded as an outstanding abstraction item, not invented.

nodes.question: What does the film or marrow describe as the dominant lymphoid population?
nodes.hint: This only chooses which marker panel to open. The immunophenotype, not the descriptor, sets the code.
nodes.coding_note: No option here emits a code. Morphology in the mature lymphoid group orients the panel; every entity in Ia2 and Ia3 is defined immunophenotypically (Pathway §3.11).

options.descriptor: Small mature lymphocytes with condensed chromatin and smudge cells
Prolymphocytes (large cells with a prominent single nucleolus) over 55% of the lymphoid population
options.coding_note: The 55% prolymphocyte threshold opens the PLL branch. Lineage is settled next: 9833 (B), 9834 (T) or 9832 for the genuinely indeterminate residual (Pathway §5.3.5).

options.descriptor: Lymphoid cells with circumferential hairy projections or villous cytoplasm
options.coding_note: Hairy cell leukaemia and splenic marginal zone lymphoma share this morphology. The B panel separates them on CD11c/CD25/CD103/CD123 and annexin-A1.

options.descriptor: Large granular lymphocytes with azurophilic granules
options.coding_note: T-lineage (9831) and NK-lineage (9948) LGL disease are different codes with different criteria — the lineage screen separates them before either is reachable.

options.descriptor: Pleomorphic cells with multilobated "flower" nuclei, with or without hypercalcaemia or lytic bone lesions
Medium-sized cells, deeply basophilic vacuolated cytoplasm, starry-sky pattern (FAB L3)
Blasts 20% or more of nucleated marrow cells
options.coding_note: Cross-tree handover (Pathway §7.1). This tree emits no precursor code.

options.descriptor: Pattern not determinable or not described

nodes.question: Which markers does the report list, and what was each result?
nodes.hint: General positivity cutoff is 10% or more of the gated lymphoid population. This node assigns lineage only — the entity panel comes next.
nodes.coding_note: TdT or CD34 positivity means this is not a mature lymphoid neoplasm: hand the case to the acute tree rather than forcing a mature code (Pathway §3.3 discriminator table). Cross-tree next_node is schema-legal — all four trees share group_01_dt.json (Pathway §7.1).

resolution_logic.coding_note: TdT is a precursor marker and is negative in every mature lymphoid entity in Ia2/Ia3. This is a precursor neoplasm — the acute tree owns it (Pathway §3.3, §7.1).
CD34 expression indicates a precursor population. Hand to the acute tree rather than coding a mature entity.
Surface light-chain restriction establishes a clonal mature B population.
Surface CD3-negative with CD16/CD56 is NK lineage (Pathway §3.11).

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: A complete lineage panel — CD19/CD20 with surface light chains, CD3/CD2/CD5/CD7, and CD16/CD56 — would open the B, T or NK entity branch.
resolution_logic.coding_note: No lineage-defining combination met. 9820 (Lymphoid leukemia, NOS) is this tree's chain-termination landing code (Pathway §6, §7.4). It must never be upgraded to an entity code on an incomplete panel.

nos_fallback.name: Lymphoid leukemia, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Mature lymphoid population recorded but no lineage-defining marker combination was met.

nodes.question: Which markers does the report list, and what was each result?
nodes.hint: CLL is CD20-dim; B-PLL and Burkitt are CD20-bright. Use Strongly positive and Weakly positive — they are what separate these entities.
nodes.coding_note: Ia2 mature B leukaemias are adult entities (Pathway §7.5) and are retained, never removed, so a genuine rare paediatric case stays codeable. Mantle cell lymphoma (cyclin D1 / SOX11 positive) is the principal CLL mimic and is a Group II entity — it is referred, not coded here.

resolution_logic.coding_note: TdT is negative in every mature B entity in Ia2. This is a precursor neoplasm — the acute tree owns it.
CD34 expression indicates a precursor population.
The full hairy cell panel (Pathway §3.11). BRAF V600E and the variant question are settled next.
CD103 is the most specific single hairy-cell marker. The confirmation node records the rest of the panel, BRAF V600E, and the HCL-variant question (Pathway §5.2).

resolution_logic.reason: CD5-positive, cyclin D1-positive clonal B cells are mantle cell lymphoma — a Group II entity, not a Group I mature B-cell leukaemia. A leukaemic phase does not move it to Group I. No Group I code is emitted; the Group II tree resolves the code.
Cyclin D1 expression in a clonal B population indicates mantle cell lymphoma, a Group II entity. No Group I code is emitted.
SOX11 expression indicates mantle cell lymphoma, including the cyclin D1-negative variant. Group II entity — no Group I code is emitted.

resolution_logic.coding_note: The classic CLL immunophenotype: CD19+ CD5+ CD23+ with dim CD20 and light-chain restriction (Pathway §3.11).
CD200 positivity with CD5/CD23 favours CLL over mantle cell lymphoma in the borderline panel.
Ki-67 above 95% with MYC protein above 80% is the accepted low-resource surrogate for MYC rearrangement (Pathway §3.3). The Burkitt screen settles it.

CD10-positive, CD5-negative, CD20-bright mature B cells raise Burkitt and the other high-grade B-cell lymphomas. The Burkitt screen settles MYC rearrangement; a non-Burkitt mature B lymphoma is a Group II entity.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: CD103 and annexin-A1, with BRAF V600E, would confirm 9940 Hairy cell leukemia, NOS.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Hairy-cell features without CD103 do not meet the hairy cell panel (Pathway §3.11). The case is not sent to B-cell prolymphocytic leukaemia, a diagnosis of exclusion, because CD19 and a bright CD20 are also present.
A CD5-negative, CD23-negative mature B leukaemia with bright CD20 and bright FMC7 raises B-PLL — a diagnosis of exclusion (Pathway §3.11).

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: Completing the ERIC/ESCCA core panel (CD19, CD5, CD20, CD23, kappa, lambda), the hairy cell panel (CD11c, CD25, CD103, CD123, annexin-A1) and cyclin D1 would resolve 9823, 9940 or refer a Group II entity.
resolution_logic.coding_note: A clonal mature B population with no entity-defining combination. 9820 is the honest NOS parent for the mature-B chain (Pathway §6: 9823 / 9940 → 9820 → 9800).

nos_fallback.name: Lymphoid leukemia, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Clonal mature B population recorded but no entity-defining marker combination was met.

nodes.question: Absolute clonal (monotypic) B-cell count in peripheral blood?
nodes.hint: The threshold is on the CLONAL B-cell count, not the total lymphocyte count. Tick 'not documented' rather than substituting the lymphocyte count.
nodes.coding_note: 5×10⁹/L is the CLL threshold (Pathway §3.11). Below it, the case is monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis, small lymphocytic lymphoma (Group II) or — only where cytopenia is attributable to marrow infiltration — CLL. The two bands are contiguous and exhaustive: a value at exactly 5.0 falls in the upper band.

bands.coding_note: The leukaemic threshold is met. Persistence and compartment are settled next.

Below the leukaemic threshold. CLL is only diagnosable here when cytopenia or disease-related symptoms are attributable to marrow infiltration; otherwise the differential is monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis or tissue-based SLL.
Count not documented. The confirmation node records that explicitly rather than assuming the threshold was met.

nos_fallback.name: Lymphoid leukemia, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Clonal B-cell count could not be banded and no CLL criterion was established.

nodes.question: What does the file document about persistence, panel completeness and compartment?
nodes.hint: The registry codes at diagnosis on the evidence then available. A shorter follow-up lowers confidence; it does not change the code.
nodes.coding_note: 9823 requires 5×10⁹/L or more clonal B cells sustained 3 months or longer plus the ERIC/ESCCA core panel (CD19, CD5, CD20, CD23, kappa, lambda); borderline phenotypes add CD43, CD79b, CD81, CD200, CD10 and ROR1 (Pathway §3.11). CLL and SLL are one entity, code 9823 — the compartment decides Group I (Ia2) or Group II (IIb2), not the code.

options.label: 5×10⁹/L or more clonal B cells sustained 3 months or longer on repeat counts, with the core panel complete
options.coding_note: The full WHO / iwCLL criterion is met and the compartment is marrow. Group I, Ia2.

options.label: 5×10⁹/L or more on a single count — fewer than 3 months of follow-up documented
options.upgrade_path: A repeat count at 3 months or more would confirm persistence. The code does not change.
options.coding_note: The registry codes at diagnosis on the evidence then available (Pathway §3.4 principle). Persistence is a confidence question, not a code question — but a single count cannot exclude a transient reactive or infection-driven clonal expansion, so confidence is medium.

options.label: Count met but the ERIC/ESCCA core panel is incomplete — CD19, CD5, CD20, CD23, kappa and lambda are not all reported
options.upgrade_path: Completing the ERIC/ESCCA core panel would resolve 9823. Borderline phenotypes add CD43, CD79b, CD81, CD200, CD10 and ROR1.
options.coding_note: A lymphocytosis with a partial panel cannot exclude mantle cell lymphoma or marginal zone lymphoma in leukaemic phase, both Group II entities. 9820 is the honest code until the panel is complete.

options.label: Clonal B-cell count not documented in the file
options.upgrade_path: An absolute clonal B-cell count would resolve 9823 (5×10⁹/L or more) or open the monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis / SLL branch (below 5×10⁹/L).
options.coding_note: The immunophenotype alone does not distinguish CLL from monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis, which is not a reportable malignancy. Do not code 9823 without the count.

options.label: Lymph-node or splenic disease is dominant; the blood and marrow involvement is secondary
options.reason: Same entity, different compartment. Nodal- or splenic-dominant CLL/SLL is small lymphocytic lymphoma and codes 9823 in Group II (IIb2), not Group I (DT master §6; Pathway §5.3). No Group I code is emitted.

nodes.question: Clonal B cells are below 5×10⁹/L. What else does the file document?
nodes.hint: Below the threshold the diagnosis turns on tissue disease and cytopenia, not on the count.
nodes.coding_note: Clonal B cells below 5×10⁹/L with no tissue disease and no cytopenia are monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis — a precursor state, not a reportable malignancy. Forcing an NOS malignant code on it would register a cancer that does not exist (nodes.md §4).

options.label: Cytopenia and/or disease-related symptoms attributable to marrow infiltration by the clonal B cells
options.coding_note: WHO-HAEM5 permits the CLL diagnosis below 5×10⁹/L when cytopenia is attributable to marrow infiltration. Record which framework was applied.

options.label: Lymphadenopathy and/or splenomegaly with tissue involvement, no cytopenia
options.reason: Tissue-based disease below the leukaemic threshold is small lymphocytic lymphoma — the same entity and the same code (9823), but Group II (IIb2). No Group I code is emitted (DT master §6).

options.label: No lymphadenopathy, no organomegaly, no cytopenia — clonal B cells only
options.reason: Monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis: clonal B cells below 5×10⁹/L with no tissue disease and no cytopenia. A precursor state, not a reportable malignancy. Re-enter if the count rises above 5×10⁹/L or tissue disease appears.

options.label: Nothing beyond the count is recorded
options.upgrade_path: Documenting nodal and splenic status, a full blood count and the marrow findings would separate CLL, small lymphocytic lymphoma (Group II) and monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis (not reportable).
options.coding_note: ⚠ Do not finalise this case on 9820 without excluding monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis — below the threshold, a clonal B population with no tissue disease and no cytopenia is not a malignancy. If the review establishes that, use the 'malignancy excluded' terminal instead.

nodes.question: What does the file record for BRAF V600E?
nodes.hint: BRAF V600E is present in classic hairy cell leukaemia and absent in HCL-variant. It changes the variant flag, never the code.
nodes.coding_note: HCL-variant and splenic B-cell lymphoma/leukaemia with prominent nucleoli have no dedicated ICD-O-3.2 code and both fall to 9940 with a variant flag (Pathway §5.2). The variant status is recorded in qualifiers and genotype_annotation — it does not change the code. This node captures the status; the next node preserves the genotype text.

options.label: BRAF V600E DETECTED (allele-specific PCR, NGS, or VE1 immunohistochemistry)
options.coding_note: Classic hairy cell leukaemia. The molecular requirement on 9940 is discharged.

options.label: BRAF V600E NOT detected — hairy-cell phenotype with a variant picture (prominent nucleoli, CD25-negative, annexin-A1-negative)
options.coding_note: The variant flag is set in qualifiers. MAP2K1 mutation is frequent in HCL-variant and is recorded as genotype annotation on the next node.

options.label: BRAF V600E not tested, or molecular testing unavailable at this facility
options.coding_note: The marker panel carries the diagnosis; BRAF is confirmatory. Molecular/PCR stays on the record as an outstanding test rather than being silently discharged.

options.label: The hairy cell panel is incomplete — CD11c, CD25, CD103, CD123 and annexin-A1 were not all reported
options.upgrade_path: Completing CD11c, CD25, CD103, CD123 and annexin-A1, plus BRAF V600E, would resolve 9940.
options.coding_note: Splenic marginal zone lymphoma with villous lymphocytes is the mimic and is a Group II entity. An incomplete panel cannot exclude it, so 9940 is not defensible.

nodes.question: Record the molecular result exactly as the report states it.
nodes.capture_label: Molecular result as reported (e.g. "BRAF V600E detected by allele-specific PCR", "BRAF V600E not detected; MAP2K1 exon 2 mutated", "not tested")
nodes.hint: The code is 9940 either way. The annotation is what preserves the variant entity, which has no code of its own.
nodes.coding_note: The genotype annotation is always persisted, even though the finding is code-neutral for 9940 — otherwise the HCL-variant / splenic B-cell lymphoma-leukaemia with prominent nucleoli entity is lost permanently (Pathway §5.2, §7.3 item 7).

resolution_logic.coding_note: Classic hairy cell leukaemia: the marker panel with BRAF V600E. Group I, Ia2.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: None — HCL-variant and splenic B-cell lymphoma/leukaemia with prominent nucleoli have no ICD-O-3.2 code of their own. The variant flag and the genotype are preserved on the case record instead; revisit if a future ICD-O revision codes them.
resolution_logic.coding_note: BRAF V600E-negative hairy cell disease is HCL-variant or splenic B-cell lymphoma/leukaemia with prominent nucleoli. Neither has a dedicated code; both fall to 9940 with the variant flag already set in qualifiers (Pathway §5.2). The variant does not change the code and must not be downgraded to 9820.
