resolution_logic.upgrade_path: BRAF V600E by allele-specific PCR, NGS or VE1 immunohistochemistry would raise confidence and settle the classic-versus-variant question.
resolution_logic.coding_note: BRAF not tested. The CD11c/CD25/CD103/CD123 and annexin-A1 panel carries the diagnosis; Molecular/PCR remains outstanding on the workup block and is deliberately not declared as satisfied.

nos_fallback.name: Lymphoid leukemia, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Hairy cell phenotype not established on review; no other mature B entity was demonstrated.

nodes.question: Which markers does the report list, and what was each result?
nodes.hint: Lineage is the whole question here. 9832 exists for the case where it genuinely cannot be established — not for the case where nobody looked.
nodes.coding_note: Registry decision §5.3.5: 9832 (PLL, NOS) is KEPT LIVE as a fallback, not retired — ICD-O-3.2 lists it Preferred/current. Prefer 9833 (B-cell) or 9834 (T-cell) whenever lineage is determinable; 9832 is for the genuinely lineage-indeterminate residual only. B-PLL is a diagnosis of exclusion: rule out CLL transformation, mantle cell lymphoma and splenic marginal zone lymphoma (Pathway §3.11).

resolution_logic.coding_note: TdT is a precursor marker — this is not a prolymphocytic leukaemia. The acute tree owns it.
CD34 expression indicates a precursor population.

resolution_logic.reason: Cyclin D1-positive clonal B cells are mantle cell lymphoma, which mimics B-PLL and must be excluded before 9833 (Pathway §3.11). Mantle cell lymphoma is a Group II entity — no Group I code is emitted.
SOX11 expression indicates mantle cell lymphoma, including the cyclin D1-negative variant. Group II entity — no Group I code is emitted.

resolution_logic.coding_note: CD103 positivity in a prolymphocytoid picture raises HCL-variant / splenic B-cell lymphoma-leukaemia with prominent nucleoli, which codes 9940 with a variant flag (Pathway §5.2) — not 9833.
Bright CD11c with CD22 in a prominent-nucleoli picture raises the hairy cell variant spectrum. Settle it before coding a prolymphocytic leukaemia.
TCL1 over-expression without B markers is the T-PLL signature.

B-lineage prolymphocytic leukaemia. A diagnosis of exclusion (ICC): CLL transformation, mantle cell lymphoma and splenic marginal zone lymphoma are ruled out by the cyclin D1/SOX11-negative, CD5/CD23-non-CLL pattern above (Pathway §3.11). Lineage is determinable, so 9833 is preferred over 9832 (§5.3.5).
B lineage established — 9833 is preferred over 9832 whenever lineage is determinable (Pathway §5.3.5).
B lineage established on CD19 with no T markers.
B lineage established on CD20 with no T markers.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: B markers (CD19, CD20, CD22, FMC7, surface light chains) or T markers (CD2, CD3, CD5, CD7, TCL1) would resolve 9833 or 9834.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Lineage genuinely indeterminate. 9832 is kept live precisely for this residual (Pathway §5.3.5) — it is not a retired code and not a placeholder for an unperformed panel. If the panel was simply not done, record that in workup_status so the case is upgradeable.

nos_fallback.name: Prolymphocytic leukemia, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Prolymphocytic leukaemia established on morphology but the lineage markers did not resolve B or T lineage.

nodes.question: What do the cytogenetics, FISH or TCL1 studies show?
nodes.hint: The third major criterion is satisfied by EITHER a 14q32/Xq28 abnormality OR TCL1/MTCP1 involvement — either one is enough.
nodes.coding_note: T-PLL major criteria (Pathway §3.11): more than 5×10⁹/L cells with a T-PLL phenotype, demonstrated T-cell clonality, AND a 14q32/Xq28 abnormality or TCL1/MTCP1 involvement. 9834's only valid downgrade is 9832 (PLL, NOS) — never 9833 and never a 'lesser T-PLL'.

options.finding: inv(14)(q11q32) or t(14;14)(q11;q32) on karyotype and/or FISH
options.coding_note: The classic T-PLL abnormality, juxtaposing TCL1 to the TCR alpha/delta locus.

options.finding: t(X;14)(q28;q11) or MTCP1 involvement on karyotype and/or FISH
options.coding_note: The Xq28/MTCP1 variant satisfies the same major criterion as 14q32.

options.finding: TCL1 protein over-expression by flow cytometry or immunohistochemistry; karyotype normal or not performed
options.coding_note: Pathway §3.11 accepts a 14q32/Xq28 abnormality OR TCL1/MTCP1 involvement — either satisfies the third major criterion. TCL1 over-expression therefore discharges the cytogenetics requirement on 9834, and the alternative is declared satisfied so a fully-subtyped case is not put on the pending worklist. A normal karyotype must not close this branch.

options.finding: Karyotype normal — no 14q32 or Xq28 abnormality — and TCL1 was NOT tested
options.upgrade_path: TCL1 by flow or immunohistochemistry, or FISH for TCL1/MTCP1, would resolve 9834. A normal karyotype alone does not exclude it.
options.coding_note: A normal karyotype with no TCL1 result leaves the third major criterion untested, so 9834 is not established. 9832 is 9834's declared NOS parent (Pathway §6: mature T 9834 → 9832) — it is the honest downgrade, not a lineage claim.

options.finding: Cytogenetics, FISH and TCL1 all unavailable at this facility, or not performed
options.upgrade_path: inv(14)/t(14;14) or t(X;14) by karyotype or FISH, or TCL1 by flow or immunohistochemistry, would resolve 9834.
options.coding_note: "Cytogenetics unavailable at UCI" is a legitimate permanent terminal state but must be recorded as such via karyotype_result_status, not passed off as a completed workup (Pathway §2.5).

nos_fallback.name: Prolymphocytic leukemia, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: T-lineage prolymphocytic leukaemia recorded but the T-PLL major criteria were not demonstrated. 9834 has no lesser T-PLL downgrade (Pathway §7.4 trap).

nodes.question: Which markers does the report list, and what was each result?
nodes.hint: No route from this node reaches 9827 directly. Every ATLL-shaped phenotype goes to the HTLV-1 gate first.
nodes.coding_note: Do not default to 9827 without confirmed HTLV-1 positivity (Pathway §6). This node routes an ATLL phenotype to the mandatory serology gate; 9827 is emitted only downstream of a confirmed-positive answer. Adult-only entities in this branch (9834) are retained per §7.5 with a soft warning, never removed.

resolution_logic.coding_note: TdT is a precursor marker and is negative in every Ia3 entity. The acute tree owns precursor T disease.
CD34 expression indicates a precursor population.
CD1a marks the cortical thymocyte stage — a precursor T neoplasm, not a mature T leukaemia.
CD4-positive, CD25-positive with loss of CD7 is the ATLL phenotype. HTLV-1 serology is mandatory and code-defining — it is asked next, and 9827 is unreachable without it.
A mature CD4+CD25+ phenotype raises ATLL. The serology gate settles it.
CD3+CD8+CD57+ is the T-LGL phenotype (Pathway §3.11). The count threshold and clonality are settled next.
A cytotoxic T phenotype with granular morphology — the T-LGL branch.
TCL1 over-expression in a mature T population is the T-PLL signature.
Surface CD3-negative with CD16/CD56 is NK lineage.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: A complete mature T/NK panel — CD2, CD3, CD4, CD5, CD7, CD8, CD25, CD57, CD16, CD56, TCL1 — with TCR clonality and HTLV-1 serology would resolve 9827, 9831, 9834 or 9948.
resolution_logic.coding_note: A mature T-cell population with no entity-defining combination. 9820 is the MANDATED landing code for an unconfirmed mature T-cell leukaemia — never 9827 (Pathway §6).

nos_fallback.name: Lymphoid leukemia, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Mature T-cell population recorded but no entity-defining marker combination was met. An unconfirmed mature T-cell leukaemia codes 9820, never 9827.

nodes.question: ATLL cannot be diagnosed without confirmed HTLV-1 positivity. What does the file record?
nodes.hint: A reactive screening assay is not a confirmed result. Only the confirmed-positive option opens the ATLL branch.
nodes.coding_note: HARD GATE. 9827 is structurally reachable only through the confirmed-positive option below — every other answer lands on 9820 or refers the case (Pathway §3.11, §6; DT master §5). Serology is recorded under Molecular/PCR in this schema's closed test vocabulary.

options.label: HTLV-1 CONFIRMED POSITIVE — screening EIA confirmed by western blot or line immunoassay, or HTLV-1 proviral DNA detected by PCR
options.coding_note: The mandatory criterion is met. The Shimoyama subtype is recorded next; it is code-neutral.

options.label: HTLV-1 serology NEGATIVE — and no alternative entity is established
options.upgrade_path: A full mature T-cell panel (TCL1, CD57, CD56, granzyme B) with TCR clonality would open 9831, 9834 or 9948.
options.coding_note: A negative HTLV-1 result EXCLUDES ATLL. The case is a mature T-cell leukaemia with no established entity, and 9820 is the mandated code (Pathway §6). 9827 is unreachable from here.

options.label: HTLV-1 NEGATIVE and the file establishes a mature T-cell lymphoma in leukaemic phase — Sézary syndrome, peripheral T-cell lymphoma, other
options.reason: Sézary syndrome and the peripheral T-cell lymphomas are Group II entities even when they circulate. HTLV-1 negativity excludes ATLL, so no Group I code is emitted; the Group II tree resolves the subtype.

options.label: HTLV-1 screening assay REACTIVE — confirmatory test pending or not performed
options.upgrade_path: A confirmatory western blot / line immunoassay, or HTLV-1 proviral DNA by PCR, would resolve 9827. Re-enter when the result returns.
options.coding_note: A reactive screening EIA is NOT confirmed positivity — indeterminate and false-reactive screens are common in this catchment. Do not code 9827 on a screen alone (Pathway §3.11).

options.label: HTLV-1 serology NOT TESTED, or unavailable at this facility
options.upgrade_path: Confirmed HTLV-1 serology would resolve 9827. Until then the case cannot be coded as ATLL at any confidence.
options.coding_note: "Do not default to 9827 without confirmed HTLV-1 positivity" (Pathway §6). An untested case lands on 9820 — this is a hard rule, not a confidence adjustment.

nodes.question: HTLV-1 is confirmed positive. Which Shimoyama subtype does the file describe?
nodes.hint: Every leukaemic subtype emits the same code. The subtype is an annotation; the compartment is what decides the group.
nodes.coding_note: Shimoyama subtypes (acute / lymphomatous / chronic / smouldering) are CODE-NEUTRAL — all remain 9827 (Pathway §1 Ia3, §3.11). 9827 is dual-group by compartment: leukaemic phase → Group I (Ia3); lymphoma phase → Group II (IIb3) (DT master §6). The lymphomatous subtype is therefore referred, not coded here — the code is the same, the group is not.

options.descriptor: Acute — leukaemic, rapidly progressive, circulating flower cells, hypercalcaemia and/or high LDH
options.coding_note: Leukaemic phase — Group I, Ia3. The subtype is stored as a display-only qualifier.

options.descriptor: Chronic — persistent lymphocytosis, indolent course
options.coding_note: Leukaemic phase — Group I, Ia3. Code-neutral subtype.

options.descriptor: Smouldering — under 5% circulating abnormal lymphocytes, skin or lung lesions, normal lymphocyte count
options.coding_note: Still 9827 and still an incident case. Indolence is prognostic, not code-defining.

options.descriptor: Lymphomatous — nodal disease dominant, under 1% circulating abnormal lymphocytes
options.reason: Lymphomatous ATLL is the lymphoma phase and routes to Group II (IIb3) by the dual-group rule (DT master §6; Pathway §1 Ia3). The code is still 9827 — the group is not Group I, so no Group I code is emitted here.

options.descriptor: Subtype not stated in the file
options.upgrade_path: Recording the Shimoyama subtype would complete the qualifier block. It does not change the code.
options.coding_note: The code is complete without the subtype. Leave shimoyama_subtype unset rather than guessing — an unrecorded qualifier is honest, an invented one is not. The compartment was established upstream as blood/marrow, so this is Group I, Ia3.

nodes.question: Absolute large granular lymphocyte (clonal T-cell) count in peripheral blood?
nodes.hint: The threshold is a sustained 0.5×10⁹/L. Tick 'not documented' rather than guessing.
nodes.coding_note: T-LGL leukaemia threshold is 0.5×10⁹/L or more, sustained (Pathway §3.11). The two bands are contiguous and exhaustive — a value at exactly 0.5 falls in the upper band. Clonality, not the count alone, is what makes the diagnosis.

bands.coding_note: Threshold met. Clonality is decisive and is settled next.

bands.upgrade_path: A sustained count of 0.5×10⁹/L or more with demonstrated TCR clonality, or a STAT3/STAT5B mutation, would resolve 9831.
bands.coding_note: Below the sustained 0.5×10⁹/L threshold the T-LGL criteria are not met (Pathway §3.11). If the review establishes that the expansion is reactive — viral, rheumatoid, post-transplant or HIV-associated — use the 'malignancy excluded' terminal instead of leaving the case on 9820.
Count not documented. Clonality is asked anyway — a demonstrated clonal LGL population with cytopenias is still T-LGL leukaemia — and the missing count is carried as an upgrade on the record.

nos_fallback.name: Lymphoid leukemia, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Large granular lymphocyte population recorded but the T-LGL count and clonality criteria were not established.

nodes.question: What does the file record for T-cell receptor clonality and STAT3/STAT5B?
nodes.hint: A polyclonal LGL expansion is reactive. Clonality is what separates a malignancy from a benign response.
nodes.coding_note: 9831 requires a demonstrated clonal population: TCR gene rearrangement by PCR/NGS, or a restricted TCR-Vβ repertoire on flow. STAT3 or STAT5B mutation is supportive and clonality-establishing (Pathway §3.11). Do not use 9831 for NK-lineage LGL disease — that is a different code with different criteria (§5.3.3).

options.label: Clonal TCR gene rearrangement demonstrated (PCR / NGS), and/or a restricted TCR-Vβ repertoire on flow
options.upgrade_path: Record the absolute LGL count if it is not already in the file — a sustained 0.5×10⁹/L or more supports the diagnosis. It does not change the code.
options.coding_note: CD3+CD8+CD57+ with demonstrated clonality. Group I, Ia3.

options.label: STAT3 or STAT5B mutation detected
options.coding_note: A somatic STAT3 or STAT5B mutation establishes clonality and is present in a substantial minority of T-LGL leukaemias (Pathway §3.11).

options.label: TCR clonality tested and POLYCLONAL, with no STAT3/STAT5B mutation
options.reason: A polyclonal large granular lymphocyte expansion is reactive — commonly viral, rheumatoid, post-transplant or HIV-associated — and is not a reportable malignancy (Pathway §4.9 principle). Re-enter if a clonal population is later demonstrated.

options.label: Clonality not tested, or molecular testing unavailable at this facility
options.upgrade_path: TCR gene rearrangement by PCR, a TCR-Vβ flow repertoire, or a STAT3/STAT5B panel would resolve 9831.
options.coding_note: An LGL phenotype without demonstrated clonality cannot be separated from a reactive expansion. 9820 is the honest code; record why via workup_status.

options.label: On review the population is NK-lineage (surface CD3-negative), not T-lineage
options.coding_note: NK-lineage LGL disease is a different code with different criteria (Pathway §3.11, §5.3.3). 9831 is a T-lineage code and must not be used for it.

nodes.question: NK-lineage large granular lymphocyte disease. Which picture does the file support?
nodes.hint: Aggressive NK-cell leukaemia and indolent NK-LGLL both code 9948. Indolence is not flagged on the code.
nodes.coding_note: Registry decision §5.3.3: indolent NK-LGLL codes 9948 UNCHANGED, with NO indolent flag — survival analysis is performed separately in biostatistics and is not derived from the morphology code. Pastoret diagnostic rule (Table 3): 3 or more major criteria, OR 2 major plus 2 minor. Major — NK count 1.0×10⁹/L or more; KIR restriction (reduced expression of 2 or more of CD158A <9%, CD158B <2%, NKB1 <4%); CD94/NKG2A over-expression; somatic STAT3/STAT5B, CCL22 or TET2 mutation without MDS-classifying alterations. Minor — other phenotypic aberration (CD161-low, activating KIR restriction); other JAK-STAT / NF-κB / PI3K mutation; sinusoidal NK infiltrate on trephine; no MDS-classifying changes.

options.label: Aggressive NK-cell leukaemia — CD3-negative, CD16+/CD56+, EBV (EBER) positive, systemic illness with fever, hepatosplenomegaly and cytopenias
options.coding_note: The defining evidence for 9948 is CD3−CD16+CD56+ with EBV positivity (Pathway §1 Ia3, §3.11). This entity occurs in adolescents and young adults and is genuinely relevant paediatrically — no adult-only warning applies.

options.label: NK-LGLL meeting the Pastoret rule — 3 or more MAJOR criteria
options.coding_note: Indolent NK-LGLL codes 9948 unchanged and carries NO indolent flag (Pathway §5.3.3). STAT3/STAT5B/CCL22/TET2 mutations are code-neutral and are recorded as annotation.

options.label: NK-LGLL meeting the Pastoret rule — 2 MAJOR plus 2 or more MINOR criteria
options.coding_note: The second limb of the verbatim diagnostic rule (Pathway §3.11). Same code, no indolent flag (§5.3.3).

options.label: Exactly 2 major criteria and NO histological (trephine) investigation
options.coding_note: Explicitly unresolved by the source (Pathway §3.11). Carry it as a distinct non-terminal state rather than forcing the call — 9948 is an aggressive-disease code and two major criteria do not support it.

options.label: CD3-negative CD16/CD56-positive population, criteria not assessed or not documented
options.upgrade_path: An absolute NK count, the KIR repertoire (CD158A, CD158B, NKB1), CD94/NKG2A, EBER and a STAT3/STAT5B panel would resolve 9948.
options.coding_note: An NK phenotype alone does not establish a neoplasm — NK expansions are common reactively. 9948 requires the criteria; 9820 is the honest code until they are documented.

options.label: On review the NK-cell expansion is reactive or transient (viral, post-transplant, chronic infection)
options.reason: A reactive or transient NK-cell expansion is not a neoplasm and is not a reportable malignancy (Pathway §4.9 principle). Re-enter if the criteria are subsequently met.

nodes.question: Two major criteria and no trephine — the source leaves this state unresolved. What can the file support now?
nodes.hint: This state is deliberately non-terminal in the source. Record what is achievable rather than forcing 9948.
nodes.coding_note: Pathway §3.11 grey zone, verbatim: "2 major criteria with no histological investigation is explicitly unresolved by the source — carry as a distinct non-terminal state rather than forcing a call." Coding 9948 here would assert an aggressive-disease code the evidence does not support.

options.label: Trephine biopsy now available and describes a sinusoidal NK infiltrate — a further criterion is met
options.coding_note: Go back and re-score against the Pastoret rule with the histological criterion included.

options.label: Trephine requested — result pending
options.upgrade_path: A trephine biopsy, and a STAT3/STAT5B panel, would complete the Pastoret criteria and resolve 9948. Result pending — re-enter when it returns.
options.coding_note: Recorded as an open workup, not as a settled diagnosis. The NK branch stays open in both directions.

options.label: Trephine not available at this facility — permanent terminal state
options.upgrade_path: Histological investigation is unavailable at this facility, so the Pastoret criteria cannot be completed and the code cannot be upgraded here.
options.coding_note: "Histology unavailable at UCI" is a legitimate permanent terminal state but must be recorded as such (Pathway §2.5), not passed off as a completed workup.

options.label: On review the NK-cell expansion is reactive or transient
options.reason: A reactive or transient NK-cell expansion is not a neoplasm and is not a reportable malignancy (Pathway §4.9 principle).

nodes.question: Which markers does the report list, and what was each result?
nodes.hint: MYC rearrangement is the gate — its absence excludes Burkitt. sIgM is unreliable in both directions and is deliberately not on this panel.
nodes.coding_note: BURKITT IS NO LONGER A GROUP I CODE. From 1 January 2021 leukaemic Burkitt codes 9687/3 in Group II (IIc); 9826/3 is retired and read-only for pre-2021 records. Registry ruling: adopt 9687, leukaemic Burkitt moves to Group II, NO Group I/II override — an override would break ICCC-3 comparability (Pathway §3.3, §5.3.11, §5.7c). This node therefore emits no Group I code on the Burkitt branch; it refers the case. 9687 does not exist in this file and must not be invented, and 9826 is terminal_reachable false and must never be emitted. Uganda-specific: endemic Burkitt is EBV-positive in about 95% with a typical jaw or facial mass; where FISH is unavailable, Ki-67 above 95% with MYC protein IHC above 80% predicts MYC rearrangement in about 99% and is the accepted surrogate.

resolution_logic.coding_note: MYC rearrangement WITH TdT positivity is MYC-rearranged B-ALL, not Burkitt — an uncoded WHO entity that falls to 9811 in the acute tree (Pathway §5.2). Do not refer this to Group II.
CD34 positivity with MYC rearrangement indicates a precursor population — MYC-rearranged B-ALL, handled by the acute tree.
MYC rearrangement with a mature, TdT-negative, CD34-negative, CD20-bright B phenotype. This is Burkitt.
MYC rearrangement with the precursor markers negative. Its absence excludes Burkitt; its presence with a mature phenotype establishes it (Pathway §3.3).
The accepted low-resource surrogate for MYC rearrangement — Ki-67 above 95% with MYC protein above 80% predicts MYC-r in about 99% (Pathway §3.3). Record that FISH was not the basis.
TdT is negative in Burkitt and positive in BCP-ALL (Pathway §3.3 discriminator table). This is a precursor neoplasm — the acute tree owns it.
CD34 is negative in Burkitt and frequently positive in BCP-ALL.
CD58 is positive in nearly all BCP-ALL and negative in Burkitt (Pathway §3.3). With no MYC rearrangement demonstrated, this is B-ALL.

The report described a Burkitt pattern and no marker overrides it. Registrar, 14 October 2026: the case reverts to what the morphology report says and takes the closest diagnosis, the Group II referral at 9687/3, which ICD-O-3.2 gives Burkitt lymphoma and its leukaemic synonyms (Pathway §3.3). The referral screen lets the clerk go back if MYC rearrangement is not established.

MYC rearrangement neither demonstrated nor surrogated, and the precursor discriminators are not recorded. Burkitt is NOT established — absence of MYC-r excludes it (Pathway §3.3) — and this tree must not emit a mature B code it cannot support. The case is an unresolved lymphoid blast population and the acute tree's morphology-only tier carries the correct code for that state. If FISH is simply unavailable, order Ki-67 and MYC protein IHC and re-enter.

nos_fallback.name: Lymphoid leukemia, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Burkitt suspected but neither MYC rearrangement nor the Ki-67/MYC-protein surrogate was demonstrated, and no other mature lymphoid entity was established. The retired number 9826 is no longer carried in Group I at all; a confirmed Burkitt is referred to Group II as 9687.

nodes.question: Marrow blast percentage (of all nucleated marrow cells)?
nodes.hint: The 25% rule historically separated Burkitt cell leukaemia from Burkitt lymphoma. Both now code 9687/3 in Group II — record the percentage for the time-series break, not to choose a group.
nodes.coding_note: Every band on this gate exits Group I. Registry ruling (Pathway §3.3, §5.3.11, §5.7c): adopt 9687 — leukaemic Burkitt moves to Group II (IIc), no Group I/II override, because an override would break ICCC-3 comparability. 9826/3 is retired and read-only for pre-2021 diagnoses; it is terminal_reachable false and must never be emitted. 9687 is a Group II code that does not exist in this file and must not be invented. Burkitt IS a malignancy — this is a referral, not a non-reportable terminal. The two numeric bands are contiguous and exhaustive: a value at exactly 25 falls in the upper band.

bands.coding_note: Leukaemic Burkitt — more than 25% marrow blasts with MYC rearrangement and a mature B phenotype. Codes 9687/3 in Group II (IIc) from 1 January 2021. 9826 is retired and read-only for earlier records; the registry adopted 9687 with no Group I/II override (Pathway §3.3, §5.3.11, §5.7c). No Group I code is emitted. ⚠ Time-series discontinuity — pre-change leukaemic Burkitt sits in Group I as 9826, post-change in Group II as 9687; flag to biostatistics for any trend analysis spanning the change.

Burkitt with marrow involvement below the 25% leukaemic threshold. This presentation was always Group II (IIc) — only the leukaemic presentation was ever 9826 / Group I — and codes 9687/3. No Group I code is emitted (Pathway §3.3).

Burkitt established on MYC rearrangement with a mature B phenotype; marrow blast percentage not documented. Both the leukaemic and the lymphoma presentation now code 9687/3 in Group II (IIc), so the missing percentage does not change the destination — record it when available for the biostatistics time-series break. No Group I code is emitted.

nos_fallback.name: Lymphoid leukemia, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Reached only by the 'uncertain subtype' escape — the abstractor was not satisfied that this is Burkitt. 9820 is the mature lymphoid NOS parent. If Burkitt IS established the case belongs in Group II as 9687 and must not be coded here.

nodes.question: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma, NOS with no subtype stated. Which topography does the file record as the primary site?
nodes.hint: This code sits in Group I or Group II purely by site. Record the site the abstractor will enter in REDCap.
nodes.coding_note: 9591 is dual-group by topography and confirmed as such by registry policy (Pathway §5.3.10, §5.5.4): C42.0 / C42.1 / C42.3 / C42.4 → Group I (Ia4); C42.2 (spleen) and every other site → Group II (IIb4). Prefer 9820 when the process is explicitly leukaemic; 9591 is for a non-Hodgkin lymphoma NOS abstracted at a Group I topography.

options.upgrade_path: Flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry and a subtype-directed panel would replace this NOS code with a specific lymphoma entity — most of which are Group II.
options.coding_note: Group I, Ia4 by topography. This is a genuine Ia4 terminal, not a Group II code borrowed (Pathway §5.5.4).

options.upgrade_path: Flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry and a subtype-directed panel would replace this NOS code with a specific entity.
options.coding_note: Group I, Ia4 by topography.

options.upgrade_path: Flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry and a subtype-directed panel would replace this NOS code with a specific entity.
options.coding_note: Group I, Ia4 by topography.

options.upgrade_path: Flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry and a subtype-directed panel would replace this NOS code with a specific entity.
options.coding_note: Group I, Ia4 by topography.

options.reason: C42.2 (spleen) is deliberately carved out of the Group I topography set for 9591 (Pathway §1 Ia4, §5.3.10). A splenic non-Hodgkin lymphoma NOS codes 9591 in Group II (IIb4). The code is the same; the group is not Group I, so no Group I code is emitted.

options.site: A nodal or extranodal site — lymph nodes, gut, skin, CNS, other
options.reason: Every site other than C42.0 / C42.1 / C42.3 / C42.4 routes 9591 to Group II (IIb4, Non-Hodgkin lymphomas NOS) (Pathway §5.3.10). No Group I code is emitted.

options.site: The process is explicitly leukaemic — circulating clonal lymphoid cells, no tissue mass
options.upgrade_path: Flow cytometry with a lineage and entity panel would resolve a specific Ia2 or Ia3 code.
options.coding_note: Prefer 9820 when the process is explicitly leukaemic — 9591's own coding note makes this the tie-break (Pathway §1 Ia4).

nodes.question: This case is Burkitt. Burkitt is not a Group I code — confirm the referral to Group II.
nodes.hint: No Group I code is emitted. Burkitt IS a malignancy, so this is a referral, not a non-reportable terminal.
nodes.coding_note: Registry ruling (Pathway §3.3, §5.3.11, §5.7c): adopt 9687 — leukaemic Burkitt moves to Group II (IIc), no Group I/II override, because an override would break ICCC-3 comparability (same reasoning as the myeloid-sarcoma question, §4.7). 9826/3 is RETIRED and read-only for pre-2021 diagnoses; it is terminal_reachable false and is never emitted. 9687/3 is a Group II code that does not exist in this file and must not be invented. The marrow blast percentage recorded on the previous node does not change the destination — only the leukaemic presentation was ever 9826 / Group I, and both presentations now code 9687/3 in Group II.

options.label: Confirm — refer this case to Group II and code 9687/3 (IIc)
options.reason: Leukaemic Burkitt codes 9687/3 in Group II (IIc) from 1 January 2021. The retired number 9826 was removed from Group I on 6 October 2026 (registrar ruling) and is no longer carried here. No Group I code is emitted, and this is NOT a non-reportable terminal — Burkitt is a malignancy and must stay on the registry, in Group II. ⚠ Time-series discontinuity — pre-change leukaemic Burkitt sits in Group I as 9826, post-change in Group II as 9687; flag to biostatistics for any trend analysis spanning the change. Every Burkitt alias string Group I used to carry is mirrored in aliases_group_02.json, so the clerk lands in Group II; verified 6 October 2026.

options.label: On review MYC rearrangement is not established — go back to the discriminator panel
options.coding_note: Absence of MYC rearrangement excludes Burkitt (Pathway §3.3). Re-score the panel: a TdT-positive, CD34-positive, CD58-positive blast population is B-ALL and belongs to the acute tree.

decision_trees.tree_label: Chronic myeloid leukaemia, myeloproliferative neoplasms and clonal eosinophilia

nodes.question: What tests are in this patient's file?
nodes.hint: This is the evidence gate. It fixes what precision is achievable and drives every 'upgrade available' line on the output block.
nodes.coding_note: Group I has no imaging-sufficient route — imaging is staging only (Pathway §0). This tree owns subgroup Ic (9863, 9875, 9876, 9950, 9960–9964) and, through its eosinophilia branch, the Ie clonal-eosinophilia codes 9965–9968. CMML and JMML belong to the MDS/JMML tree; acute leukaemia (blasts ≥20%) belongs to the acute tree unless BCR::ABL1 is positive, in which case a blast-phase CML stays here as 9875.

options.label: Referral / clinical note only — no blood film or marrow report
Blood film, marrow aspirate or trephine morphology only — no gene test
Morphology and a karyotype
Morphology and FISH, no karyotype
Morphology and PCR, no karyotype or FISH
Morphology and sequencing, no karyotype, FISH or PCR
Hypereosinophilia is the dominant finding, whatever else is in the file
options.coding_note: The eosinophilia cascade starts at a HARD GATE, not at a laboratory result. In the UCI catchment hypereosinophilia is overwhelmingly parasitic or HIV-related; skipping the exclusion step is the largest single false-positive cancer-registration risk in Group I (Pathway §3.10).

options.label: Monocytosis-predominant picture — persistent monocytosis with or without splenomegaly
options.coding_note: CMML (9945), JMML (9946) and MDS/MPN-U (9975) are owned by the MDS/JMML tree (Pathway §7.1). Hand the case over rather than coding a monocytic entity here. A Ph-POSITIVE monocytic case is the exception — that is CML and comes back to this tree.

options.label: Malignancy excluded on review — reactive, non-neoplastic or the diagnosis was revised
options.reason: The abstractor recorded that this case is not a reportable malignancy. No morphology code is emitted and the case leaves the malignant registry.

nodes.question: What exactly does the referral or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: A referral naming CML is not a BCR::ABL1 result. The wording chooses the code, and at this tier the code is a placeholder.
nodes.coding_note: Referral-only tier: confidence is LOW and every downstream test is listed as an upgrade. 9863 is the "BCR::ABL1 pending" placeholder and never a positive diagnosis (Pathway §3.9) — record why via workup_status and karyotype_result_status.

options.label: Note reads "CML", "chronic myeloid leukaemia" or "chronic granulocytic leukaemia" — no BCR::ABL1 result in the file
options.upgrade_path: A Philadelphia chromosome on karyotype, BCR::ABL1 FISH or RT-PCR would upgrade this to 9875.
options.coding_note: 9863 is a PLACEHOLDER — "BCR::ABL1 pending". It must never be reported as a confirmed CML. If BCR::ABL1 later returns negative the case is reassessed against atypical CML (9876) and the other MPN entities, not left on 9863.

options.label: Note reads "CML in blast crisis" / "blast phase" — no BCR::ABL1 result in the file
options.upgrade_path: BCR::ABL1 by FISH or RT-PCR would upgrade this to 9875. The phase does not change the code either way.
options.coding_note: Phase is NOT a code (Pathway §3.9). A blast crisis without a BCR::ABL1 result is still the 9863 placeholder, not an acute-leukaemia code; once BCR::ABL1 is confirmed positive the code is 9875 whatever the blast percentage. Record the phase as a display-only qualifier.

options.label: Note reads "myeloproliferative disorder", "MPN", "polycythaemia", "essential thrombocythaemia" or "myelofibrosis" — no marrow, no driver mutation
options.upgrade_path: A marrow trephine with a graded reticulin stain and a JAK2 / CALR / MPL driver panel would resolve 9950, 9961 or 9962.
options.coding_note: The named entities each require a driver mutation plus a phenotype threshold (Pathway §1, Ic). A referral word is not that evidence — 9960 is the honest code.

options.label: Note reads only "leukaemia" — neither acuity nor lineage stated
options.upgrade_path: A blood film and a blast count would establish acuity and lineage.
options.coding_note: Root chain-termination code (Pathway §6: CML 9875 → 9863 → 9960 → 9800). Neither 9863 nor 9960 is defensible on this wording.

nodes.question: What does the blood film / marrow aspirate report describe?
nodes.hint: Cytochemistry and a manual differential count as morphology, not as cytogenetics.
nodes.coding_note: Morphology-only tier: placeholder and NOS-parent codes, confidence MEDIUM. Cytogenetics / FISH is the upgrade for every branch here.

options.label: Marked leucocytosis with a full myeloid left shift, basophilia and splenomegaly — the classic CML film, no genetics in the file
options.upgrade_path: A Philadelphia chromosome on karyotype, or BCR::ABL1 by FISH or RT-PCR, would upgrade this to 9875.
options.coding_note: 9863 is the "BCR::ABL1 pending" placeholder (Pathway §3.9). A classic film is a strong clinical impression, not a molecular result — basophils <2% distinguishes atypical CML from CML but is not itself a criterion.

options.label: Neutrophilic or myeloproliferative picture, entity not determinable on morphology alone
options.upgrade_path: BCR::ABL1 (FISH or RT-PCR), a karyotype, and a JAK2 / CALR / MPL / CSF3R panel would resolve 9875, 9876, 9950, 9961, 9962 or 9963.
options.coding_note: 9960 is the chain-termination NOS parent for subgroup Ic (Pathway §6, §7.4).

options.label: Hypereosinophilia is the dominant abnormality
Monocytosis is the dominant abnormality — monocytes ≥0.5×10⁹/L and ≥10% of WBC
options.coding_note: CMML and JMML are owned by the MDS/JMML tree (Pathway §7.1). Reactive monocytosis — TB, HIV, other chronic infection — is the commonest cause in the UCI catchment and that tree carries the exclusion.

options.label: Film reviewed — the leucocytosis is reactive (infection, inflammation, steroids, post-splenectomy)
options.reason: The blood picture is reactive, not a myeloproliferative neoplasm. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).

nodes.question: What does the cytogenetics / FISH / molecular report say about BCR::ABL1?
nodes.hint: This is the master fork of the tree. Everything Ph-positive is CML; everything Ph-negative is assessed on its blood and marrow picture.
nodes.coding_note: BCR::ABL1 positive is 9875 REGARDLESS OF PHASE (Pathway §3.9). 9863 is reachable from here ONLY as the "BCR::ABL1 pending" placeholder — never as the answer for a case whose BCR::ABL1 came back positive. There is no valid downgrade from 9875 to a lesser CML code, so this node's NOS fallback is 9960 (Pathway §7.4).

options.finding: Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22)(q34;q11.2) on karyotype, and/or BCR::ABL1 positive on FISH
options.coding_note: Ph-positive. The next step records the phase as a display-only qualifier; it does not change the code.

options.finding: BCR::ABL1 transcript detected by RT-PCR (p210 and/or p190), with or without a karyotype
options.coding_note: The transcript isoform (p190 / p210 / p230) is code-neutral — record it in genotype_annotation. A variant or masked Philadelphia translocation is RT-PCR- or FISH-detectable when the karyotype looks normal.

options.finding: BCR::ABL1 NEGATIVE — FISH and/or RT-PCR performed and negative
options.coding_note: BCR::ABL1 is properly excluded, so the Ph-negative entities (9876, 9950, 9961–9964) are now reachable on their own criteria.

options.finding: Karyotype normal / no Philadelphia chromosome seen — FISH and RT-PCR NOT performed
options.coding_note: A normal karyotype does not exclude BCR::ABL1: variant three-way translocations and masked / cryptic insertions are invisible on karyotype and need FISH or RT-PCR. Do not resolve to a Ph-negative entity yet.

options.finding: BCR::ABL1 testing not performed, or unavailable at this facility
options.upgrade_path: BCR::ABL1 by FISH or RT-PCR would resolve this to 9875 if positive, or open the Ph-negative branch (9876, 9950, 9961–9964) if negative.
options.coding_note: This is the ONE legitimate use of 9863 — "BCR::ABL1 pending" (Pathway §3.9). "Molecular unavailable at UCI" is a legitimate permanent terminal state but must be recorded as such via karyotype_result_status, not passed off as a completed workup.

nos_fallback.name: Myeloproliferative neoplasm, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Chronic myeloproliferative picture recorded but no specific entity could be established. 9875 has no valid downgrade to a lesser CML code (Pathway §7.4).

nodes.question: A normal karyotype cannot exclude BCR::ABL1. Has FISH or RT-PCR been performed since?
nodes.hint: This branch deliberately cannot close to a Ph-negative diagnosis. It closes to the 9863 placeholder with the missing test named on the record.
nodes.coding_note: Variant t(9;22) translocations and masked insertions of ABL1 into BCR are cryptic on karyotype. Closing to atypical CML (9876) or to an MPN entity on a normal karyotype alone would mis-code a treatable, TKI-responsive disease (Pathway §3.9).

options.label: FISH / RT-PCR now available — go back and enter the result
FISH / RT-PCR requested — result pending
FISH / RT-PCR not available at this facility

nodes.question: Record why BCR::ABL1 could not be tested. The case codes 9863 with the missing test named.
nodes.hint: 9863 here is an honest pending-workup placeholder, not a diagnosis of CML.
nodes.coding_note: A case coded on the placeholder must record WHY, via karyotype_result_status (pending / not done / unavailable / declined). "Cytogenetics unavailable at UCI" is a legitimate permanent terminal state (Pathway §2.5).

options.label: Pending — record now and re-enter the tool when the result returns
options.upgrade_path: BCR::ABL1 by FISH or RT-PCR would upgrade this to 9875, or open the Ph-negative branch. Result pending — re-enter when it returns.
options.coding_note: Do not treat this as a settled diagnosis of CML. The BCR::ABL1 branch is still open in both directions.

options.label: Not available at this facility — permanent terminal state
options.upgrade_path: BCR::ABL1 FISH and RT-PCR are unavailable; the code cannot be upgraded at this facility.
options.coding_note: Recorded as a permanent unavailable-workup terminal, not as an excluded BCR::ABL1.

options.label: Test declined or not done for another reason
options.upgrade_path: BCR::ABL1 by FISH or RT-PCR would resolve the case; the test was not done.

nodes.question: BCR::ABL1 is positive, so the code is 9875. What blast percentage does the file record, so the phase can be stored as a qualifier?
nodes.hint: Every option on this node emits the SAME code. You are recording staging, not choosing a diagnosis.
nodes.coding_note: PHASE IS NOT A CODE (Pathway §3.9, §5.1). Chronic, accelerated and blast phase all code 9875; cml_phase is display-only and must never appear in resolution logic. Registry phase definition is WHO 2022 — blast % only, chronic <20%, blast phase ≥20%, no accelerated tier. A blast-phase CML must NOT be re-coded as an acute leukaemia: 9875 stays, whatever the blast count and whatever the blast lineage.

options.descriptor: Blasts under 10% in blood and marrow — chronic phase on every definition
options.coding_note: Chronic phase. Recorded as a qualifier only.

options.descriptor: Blasts 10–19% in blood or marrow
options.coding_note: Divergent staging, identical code. ICC 2022 and ELN call this accelerated phase; the registry's ratified definition is WHO 2022, which has no accelerated tier and calls this chronic phase. Either way the code is 9875 — record which framework was applied.

options.descriptor: Blasts 20% or more in blood or marrow — blast phase (myeloid or lymphoid blast crisis)
options.coding_note: Blast phase is still 9875. Do NOT route this case to the acute-leukaemia tree and do NOT code 9812, 9861 or 9912. A lymphoid blast crisis with a documented preceding chronic phase is CML in lymphoid blast phase, not de novo BCR::ABL1-positive B-ALL (Pathway §3.9). If no preceding chronic phase is documented and the presentation is de novo acute, use the acute tree instead — that is a clinical judgement about the history, never about the blast count.

options.descriptor: Blast percentage not documented in the file
options.upgrade_path: A blast count on blood and marrow would let the phase qualifier be recorded. It does not change the code.
options.coding_note: The code is complete without the phase. Leave cml_phase unset rather than guessing — an unrecorded qualifier is honest, an invented one is not.

nodes.question: BCR::ABL1 is excluded. Which picture do the blood film and marrow describe?
nodes.hint: Pick the dominant abnormality. Eosinophilia and monocytosis take priority over neutrophilia when both are present, because each carries its own mandatory exclusion.
nodes.coding_note: With BCR::ABL1 excluded, the Ph-negative Ic entities separate on the blood picture: dysplastic neutrophilia → atypical CML (9876); mature neutrophilia → CNL (9963); erythrocytosis / thrombocytosis / fibrosis → the driver-mutation entities (9950, 9961, 9962). 9950, 9961, 9962 and 9963 are vanishingly rare in children and carry an age-implausibility warning — they stay reachable so genuine rare paediatric cases remain codeable (Pathway §7.5).

options.descriptor: Neutrophilic leucocytosis WITH dysgranulopoiesis — immature granulocytes ≥10% of WBC, blasts <20%, eosinophils <10%, monocytes <10%
options.coding_note: Atypical CML territory (9876). Dysgranulopoiesis is the discriminator against CNL.

options.descriptor: Sustained MATURE neutrophilia — segmented plus banded neutrophils ≥80% of WBC, precursors <10%, no significant dysgranulopoiesis, monocytes <10%, blasts rare
options.coding_note: Chronic neutrophilic leukaemia territory (9963). The shared criteria are met; the next node applies the disjunctive WBC gate (Pathway §3.9).

options.descriptor: Erythrocytosis, thrombocytosis, or a fibrotic marrow with megakaryocyte atypia
options.coding_note: The classic Ph-negative MPN triad: polycythaemia vera (9950), essential thrombocythaemia (9962), primary myelofibrosis (9961). Each needs a phenotype threshold AND a driver mutation.

options.descriptor: Hypereosinophilia — eosinophils ≥10% of WBC and/or a persistently raised absolute eosinophil count
options.coding_note: The clonal-eosinophilia cascade (9964–9968) begins at a hard secondary-cause gate, never at a laboratory result (Pathway §3.10).

options.descriptor: Monocytosis — monocytes ≥0.5×10⁹/L and ≥10% of WBC
options.coding_note: CMML (9945), JMML (9946) and MDS/MPN-U (9975) are owned by the MDS/JMML tree (Pathway §7.1). BCR::ABL1 has already been excluded, which is one of that tree's mandatory JMML criteria.

options.descriptor: A myeloproliferative picture that fits none of the above, or the marrow detail needed to choose is not in the file
options.upgrade_path: A trephine with a graded reticulin stain, a full differential count, and a JAK2 / CALR / MPL / CSF3R panel would resolve 9876, 9950, 9961, 9962 or 9963.
options.coding_note: 9960 is the chain-termination NOS parent for subgroup Ic (Pathway §6, §7.4). Record why via workup_status.

options.descriptor: Reviewed — the picture is reactive or the diagnosis was revised
options.reason: Reviewed as a reactive blood picture rather than a myeloproliferative neoplasm. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).

nodes.question: Atypical CML has a closed criteria list. Which statement matches the file?
nodes.hint: SETBP1 and ETNK1 are supportive, not required. Basophils <2% distinguishes atypical CML from CML but is not itself a formal criterion.
nodes.coding_note: Criteria (Pathway §3.9): WBC ≥13×10⁹/L with immature myeloid cells ≥10% of WBC · PB/BM blasts <20% · dysgranulopoiesis · eosinophils <10% · monocytes <10% · hypercellular marrow with granulocytic hyperplasia and dysplasia · BCR::ABL1 and the M/LN-eo kinase fusions excluded. WHO-HAEM5 renames the entity "MDS/MPN with neutrophilia"; ICC keeps "atypical CML" — naming only, same code 9876 (Pathway §5.4).

options.label: All criteria met AND an MDS-qualifying cytopenia is present
options.coding_note: Both WHO-HAEM5 and ICC-2022 classify this case identically — no arbitration needed. BCR::ABL1 exclusion by FISH or RT-PCR discharges the molecular requirement.

options.label: All criteria met but there is NO MDS-qualifying cytopenia
options.coding_note: Divergent rule (Pathway §5.4). WHO-HAEM5 requires no cytopenia and classifies this as MDS/MPN with neutrophilia = 9876. ICC-2022 additionally requires an MDS-qualifying cytopenia and would not classify it as atypical CML. The registry codes 9876 and records which framework was applied.

options.label: Eosinophils are 10% or more of the WBC
options.coding_note: Eosinophils ≥10% fails an atypical CML criterion and opens the myeloid/lymphoid-neoplasm-with-eosinophilia cascade, which atypical CML explicitly excludes (Pathway §3.9, §3.10).

options.label: Monocytes are 10% or more of the WBC
options.coding_note: Monocytes ≥10% fails an atypical CML criterion and puts the case in CMML territory, owned by the MDS/JMML tree (Pathway §3.9, §7.1).

options.label: The PDGFRA / PDGFRB / FGFR1 / PCM1::JAK2 kinase fusions have NOT been excluded, or the dysplasia assessment is missing
options.upgrade_path: FISH or RT-PCR for the M/LN-eo kinase fusions, and a documented dysgranulopoiesis assessment, would establish or exclude 9876.
options.coding_note: Exclusion of the kinase fusions is part of the atypical CML definition. Until it is documented, 9876 is not defensible and 9960 is the honest NOS parent (Pathway §3.9, §6).

options.label: Reviewed — the neutrophilia is reactive or the diagnosis was revised
options.reason: Reviewed as a reactive neutrophilia rather than atypical CML. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).

nodes.question: Total white cell count?
nodes.hint: Value in ×10⁹/L. Tick 'not documented' rather than guessing.
nodes.coding_note: THE GATE IS A DISJUNCTION and the registry adopts BOTH routes (Pathway §3.9, §5.4). Route A — WBC ≥25×10⁹/L, no molecular test required (WHO-HAEM5; ICC too when CSF3R is negative). Route B — WBC ≥13×10⁹/L with an activating CSF3R mutation (ICC only). The shared criteria (neutrophils ≥80%, precursors <10%, no dysgranulopoiesis, monocytes <10%, blasts rare, normal maturation, BCR::ABL1/PV/ET/PMF/M-LN-eo excluded) were confirmed at the previous node.

override_when.coding_note: BCR::ABL1-positive disease is CML (9875), and its exclusion is a shared CNL criterion. A Ph-positive case can never be CNL, whatever the white count (Pathway §3.9).

bands.coding_note: Route A — count alone. WHO-HAEM5 accepts ≥25×10⁹/L unconditionally and ICC accepts it too when CSF3R is negative, so no molecular result is required. Phase is not a code here either: 10–19% blasts is accelerated phase, ≥20% is blast phase — both stay 9963.
Route B territory — ICC only, and only with an activating CSF3R mutation (or the ICC non-molecular alternative). WHO-HAEM5 would not call this CNL at all.

bands.upgrade_path: A repeat full blood count documenting persistent neutrophilia would establish whether either CNL route's threshold is met.
bands.coding_note: Below BOTH routes' thresholds — this is not CNL under either classification. If the marrow nonetheless documents a myeloproliferative process, 9960 is the honest code; if the neutrophilia is reactive, use the not-a-reportable-malignancy terminal on the previous node instead.

bands.upgrade_path: A full blood count with a differential would apply the CNL threshold and could resolve this to 9963.
bands.coding_note: The white count is the gate. Undocumented means the gate cannot be applied — 9960, not 9963.

nos_fallback.name: Myeloproliferative neoplasm, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Chronic myeloproliferative picture recorded but no specific entity could be established. 9875 has no valid downgrade to a lesser CML code (Pathway §7.4).

nodes.question: WBC is 13–24×10⁹/L, so ICC route B applies. What does the file show for CSF3R?
nodes.hint: Route B is the only way to reach 9963 below 25×10⁹/L, and it is an ICC-2022 rule.
nodes.coding_note: ICC route B: WBC ≥13×10⁹/L WITH an activating CSF3R mutation (typically T618I). ICC also allows a non-molecular alternative where CSF3R is unavailable: persistent neutrophilia for ≥3 months, splenomegaly, and reactive causes excluded — including demonstrated clonality if a plasma-cell neoplasm is present (Pathway §3.9).

options.finding: Activating CSF3R mutation present (e.g. T618I)
options.coding_note: ICC route B satisfied. WHO-HAEM5 would not classify this as CNL at this white count — record which framework was applied (Pathway §5.4).

options.finding: CSF3R unavailable, BUT persistent neutrophilia for ≥3 months, splenomegaly, and documented exclusion of reactive causes
options.coding_note: ICC's explicit non-molecular alternative for settings where CSF3R testing is not available (Pathway §3.9). The clinical constellation discharges the molecular requirement; record that CSF3R itself was never performed.

options.finding: CSF3R tested and NEGATIVE
options.upgrade_path: None on this route. ICC requires ≥25×10⁹/L when CSF3R is negative; a rising white count on repeat testing would re-open the CNL question.
options.coding_note: CSF3R-negative at 13–24×10⁹/L fails BOTH routes — ICC then requires ≥25×10⁹/L, and WHO-HAEM5 always does. 9963 is not defensible; 9960 is the honest NOS parent (Pathway §3.9).

options.finding: CSF3R not performed, and the non-molecular alternative is not documented
options.upgrade_path: CSF3R sequencing, or documentation of ≥3 months of neutrophilia with splenomegaly and reactive causes excluded, would establish 9963 on ICC route B.
options.coding_note: Route B is unestablished. "Molecular unavailable at UCI" is a legitimate permanent terminal state but must be recorded as such (Pathway §2.5).

options.finding: Reviewed — the neutrophilia has a documented reactive cause (infection, chronic inflammation, corticosteroids, G-CSF)
options.reason: The neutrophilia is reactive. Exclusion of reactive causes is a shared CNL criterion under both classifications, so this is not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §3.9, §4.9).

nos_fallback.name: Myeloproliferative neoplasm, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Chronic myeloproliferative picture recorded but no specific entity could be established. 9875 has no valid downgrade to a lesser CML code (Pathway §7.4).

nodes.question: Which phenotype-plus-driver combination does the file document?
nodes.hint: Each of these entities needs BOTH a phenotype threshold and a driver mutation. One without the other does not reach the code.
nodes.coding_note: Polycythaemia vera, essential thrombocythaemia and primary myelofibrosis are vanishingly rare in children (Pathway §1, Ic). They stay reachable — removing them would make a genuine rare paediatric case uncodeable — but every option carries the age-implausibility warning and should be confirmed independently before finalising (Pathway §7.5).

options.finding: Erythrocytosis above threshold (Hb >16.5 g/dL male / >16.0 g/dL female, or Hct >49% male / >48% female) WITH a JAK2 V617F or JAK2 exon-12 mutation
options.coding_note: Polycythaemia vera. Paediatric erythrocytosis is far more often congenital (EPO-receptor, high-affinity haemoglobin, hypoxia) — a JAK2 mutation is what separates PV from those, and it is required here.

options.finding: Platelets ≥450×10⁹/L WITH a JAK2, CALR or MPL mutation
options.coding_note: Essential thrombocythaemia. Reactive thrombocytosis — iron deficiency, infection, inflammation, post-splenectomy — is far commoner in children and is excluded by the driver requirement.

options.finding: Trephine megakaryocyte atypia with a GRADED reticulin / collagen stain WITH a JAK2, CALR or MPL mutation
options.coding_note: Primary myelofibrosis. The trephine and the graded reticulin stain are both required — an aspirate alone cannot support this code.

options.finding: The phenotype is present but the JAK2 / CALR / MPL panel was NEGATIVE or was not performed
options.upgrade_path: A JAK2 V617F and exon-12, CALR and MPL panel would resolve this to 9950, 9961 or 9962.
options.coding_note: A driver mutation is required for all three entities. Triple-negative primary myelofibrosis exists in adults but needs another clonal marker plus exclusion of reactive marrow fibrosis — in a child, refer for senior review and use the uncertain-subtype escape rather than assuming it. 9960 is the honest code here.

options.finding: Reviewed — secondary or reactive erythrocytosis, thrombocytosis or marrow fibrosis (hypoxia, congenital polycythaemia, iron deficiency, infection, inflammation, post-splenectomy)
options.reason: The blood or marrow finding has a documented reactive or congenital cause. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).

nos_fallback.name: Myeloproliferative neoplasm, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Chronic myeloproliferative picture recorded but no specific entity could be established. 9875 has no valid downgrade to a lesser CML code (Pathway §7.4).

nodes.question: HARD GATE. Before ANY clonal-eosinophilia code, the file must document exclusion of parasitic infection AND HIV. What does it show?
nodes.hint: This gate is not optional and cannot be skipped. Answer from what is written in the file, not from clinical impression.
nodes.coding_note: STEP 1 OF THE CASCADE IS A HARD GATE (Pathway §3.10, §5.6). Secondary causes to exclude: parasitic (strongyloides, schistosoma, filariasis, hookworm, toxocara), HIV, drugs, allergy, autoimmune disease and solid-tumour-associated eosinophilia. In the UCI catchment hypereosinophilia is overwhelmingly parasitic or HIV-related; skipping this step is the largest single false-positive cancer-registration risk in Group I. An unresolved secondary cause must reach a non-reportable terminal, never a myeloid-neoplasm code.

options.label: BOTH excluded and documented — stool microscopy and/or serology negative for the parasitic set, AND an HIV test is negative; drugs, allergy, autoimmune disease and solid tumour also considered
options.coding_note: The hard gate is satisfied. Only now do the clonal-eosinophilia codes (9964–9968) become reachable.

options.label: A secondary cause has been IDENTIFIED — parasitic infection, HIV, a drug reaction, allergy, autoimmune disease or a solid tumour
options.reason: The hypereosinophilia has a documented secondary cause. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted. This is the commonest false-positive registration risk in Group I in the UCI catchment (Pathway §3.10, §4.9).

options.label: Parasitic infection excluded, but HIV status is unknown or not tested
options.coding_note: Half a gate is not a gate. HIV-associated eosinophilia is common in this catchment and the exclusion must be documented before any clonal code.

options.label: HIV excluded, but no parasitic screen has been performed
options.coding_note: Half a gate is not a gate. The parasitic screen must be documented before any clonal code.

options.label: Neither has been assessed
options.coding_note: The gate has not been attempted. No clonal-eosinophilia code is reachable from here.

nodes.question: The secondary-cause exclusion is incomplete, so no myeloid-neoplasm code can be emitted. What is the status of the missing test?
nodes.hint: This branch deliberately cannot reach a morphology code. It exists so the case is recorded honestly and can be re-entered when the screen is done.
nodes.coding_note: An unresolved secondary cause must reach a NON-REPORTABLE terminal, not a myeloid-neoplasm code (Pathway §3.10, §5.6, §4.9). Coding 9964–9968 here would register a cancer that has not been established. If a senior pathologist judges the case neoplastic on other grounds, use the uncertain-subtype escape hatch rather than this branch.

options.label: The parasitic screen / HIV test is now available — go back and enter the result
Screening requested — result pending
options.reason: The secondary-cause exclusion required before any clonal-eosinophilia code is still pending. Not reportable on the present evidence — no code is emitted. Re-enter the tool when the parasitic screen and HIV result return (Pathway §3.10).

options.label: Screening not available at this facility
options.reason: The parasitic screen and/or HIV test that the hard gate requires is unavailable, so a secondary cause cannot be excluded. Not reportable — no code is emitted. In this catchment an unexcluded secondary cause is far more likely than a clonal eosinophilic neoplasm (Pathway §3.10, §4.9).

nodes.question: Secondary causes are excluded. What clonality evidence does the file contain?
nodes.hint: Idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome and a clonal eosinophilic neoplasm look identical on the film — clonality is what separates them.
nodes.coding_note: Cascade step 5 is asked BEFORE the fusion dropdown, because the dropdown's NOS fallback is 9964 and 9964 requires demonstrated clonality (ICC, Pathway §5.4). Without clonality the case is idiopathic HES and is NOT REPORTABLE (Pathway §3.10, §4.9). A normal karyotype is not "tested and normal" for this purpose — FIP1L1::PDGFRA is cryptic and needs FISH for the CHIC2 deletion or RT-PCR.

options.label: A clonal abnormality is demonstrated, or specific fusion testing has been performed — an abnormal karyotype, a kinase fusion, another clonal molecular marker, or an increased blast count
options.coding_note: Clonality established (or specific fusion testing done). The cascade can now resolve the specific entity.

options.label: Karyotype normal, but FISH for the CHIC2 deletion / RT-PCR for FIP1L1::PDGFRA has NOT been performed
options.coding_note: A normal karyotype closes nothing here. FIP1L1::PDGFRA is a cryptic deletion, invisible on karyotype, and the resulting disease is imatinib-responsive — the most consequential miss in this branch (Pathway §4.4, §5.6).

options.label: Cytogenetics AND molecular testing performed and completely normal — including FISH for the CHIC2 deletion or RT-PCR for FIP1L1::PDGFRA — with no clonal marker and no increased blasts
options.reason: Persistent hypereosinophilia with secondary causes excluded and no demonstrable clonality is idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome. HES is not a malignancy — no code is emitted, and in particular not 9964 (Pathway §3.10 step 5, §4.9).

options.label: No cytogenetic or molecular testing has been performed at all
Reviewed — the hypereosinophilia is reactive or the diagnosis was revised
options.reason: Reviewed as reactive or non-neoplastic hypereosinophilia. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).

nodes.question: No clonality testing has been done. What is its status?
nodes.hint: Untested is not the same as negative — but neither is it evidence of a neoplasm.
nodes.coding_note: CEL (9964) requires demonstrated clonality under the registry's ratified ICC criteria (Pathway §5.4). With no testing at all, clonality is unestablished and the case cannot be coded as a myeloid neoplasm; the honest record is a non-reportable terminal naming the missing tests. If a senior pathologist judges the case neoplastic on other grounds, use the uncertain-subtype escape hatch, which lands on the nearest NOS code with a discordance flag.

options.label: Karyotype / FISH / RT-PCR now available — go back and enter the result
Testing requested — result pending
options.reason: Clonality is unestablished and the fusion cascade is untested. Not reportable on the present evidence — no code is emitted. Re-enter the tool when the karyotype, FISH (CHIC2) or RT-PCR result returns (Pathway §3.10).

options.label: Cytogenetics and molecular testing not available at this facility
options.reason: Clonality cannot be demonstrated at this facility, and CEL (9964) requires demonstrated clonality. Recorded as not reportable with the missing tests named, rather than as an unproven myeloid neoplasm (Pathway §3.10, §4.9, §5.4).

nodes.question: Which finding does the cytogenetics / FISH / molecular report give?
nodes.hint: Work down the list in order. The detection method shown under each choice is the method that finding actually requires.
nodes.coding_note: Cascade order (Pathway §3.10): FIP1L1::PDGFRA → 9965, then karyotype 5q31-33 PDGFRB → 9966 and 8p11-12 FGFR1 → 9967, then PCM1::JAK2 → 9968, then clonality without a named fusion → 9964. The secondary-cause hard gate and the clonality gate are both upstream of this node and cannot be bypassed.

options.finding: FIP1L1::PDGFRA — CHIC2 deletion on FISH, or RT-PCR positive (or another PDGFRA rearrangement with a variant partner)
options.coding_note: CRYPTIC — never visible on karyotype. Only FISH for the CHIC2 deletion or RT-PCR can establish or exclude it, and either method alone is sufficient. Clinically the most important call in this branch: these cases are imatinib-responsive (Pathway §4.4, §5.6).

options.finding: PDGFRB rearrangement — 5q31-33 abnormality on karyotype, confirmed by FISH
options.coding_note: Visible on karyotype as a 5q31-33 rearrangement; FISH confirms the partner. Also imatinib-responsive.

options.finding: FGFR1 abnormality — 8p11-12 rearrangement on karyotype, confirmed by FISH
options.coding_note: 8p11-12 myeloproliferative syndrome. Not imatinib-responsive — the distinction from PDGFRA/PDGFRB matters clinically as well as for coding.

options.finding: PCM1::JAK2 — t(8;9)(p22;p24) on karyotype, or FISH, or RT-PCR positive
options.coding_note: 9968 became a live ICD-O-3.2 code at the 3.2 revision and was previously (and wrongly) advised to 9964 (Pathway §5.7). REGISTRY ACTION OUTSTANDING: no REDCap dropdown option exists for this code yet, so the clerk cannot select it in REDCap until one is added.

options.finding: ETV6::ABL1, a FLT3 fusion, or another kinase fusion with no dedicated ICD-O-3.2 code
options.coding_note: No ICD-O-3.2 code exists for these. They land provisionally on 9964 with the genotype preserved, or the information is lost permanently (Pathway §5.2).

options.finding: Karyotype normal, blasts increased as the only evidence of clonality, and FISH for the CHIC2 deletion / RT-PCR for FIP1L1::PDGFRA NOT performed
options.coding_note: Clonality rests on the blast count alone and the karyotype is normal, so the cryptic branch stays open and 9964 is not assigned (Pathway §4.4, §5.6).

options.finding: Karyotype ABNORMAL (a clonal abnormality is shown), but FISH for the CHIC2 deletion / RT-PCR for FIP1L1::PDGFRA NOT performed
options.coding_note: Clonality is demonstrated with secondary causes excluded, so the case codes 9964 (Pathway §3.10 step 5). The bar on 9964 in §5.6 applies on a normal karyotype.

options.finding: Karyotype done AND FISH / RT-PCR negative for the whole kinase-fusion set, with clonality shown by another marker or by increased blasts
options.coding_note: Chronic eosinophilic leukaemia, NOS — the properly closed terminal. Registry applies ICC criteria for CEL versus HES: ≥10% peripheral eosinophils, clonality required, blast increase supportive (Pathway §5.4). The cryptic branch has been closed by an adequate method, so this is a defensible terminal and not an incomplete workup.

nos_fallback.name: Chronic eosinophilic leukemia
nos_fallback.reason: Clonal hypereosinophilia with the secondary causes excluded, but no specific kinase fusion identified.

nodes.question: A normal karyotype cannot exclude FIP1L1::PDGFRA. Has FISH for the CHIC2 deletion or RT-PCR been performed since?
nodes.hint: This branch deliberately cannot close to 9964. It closes to the MPN NOS parent only with the missing test named on the record.
nodes.coding_note: FIP1L1::PDGFRA arises from an interstitial 4q12 deletion that removes CHIC2 — there is no karyotypic abnormality to see. A normal karyotype must never close this branch, and must never resolve to 9964 (Pathway §4.4, §5.6, §7.5).

options.label: FISH (CHIC2) / RT-PCR now available — go back and enter the result
FISH / RT-PCR requested — result pending
FISH / RT-PCR not available at this facility

nodes.question: Record why FIP1L1::PDGFRA could not be tested. The case codes 9960 with the missing test named.
nodes.hint: 9960, not 9964: the alert forbids assigning 9964 on a normal karyotype, so the case steps one rung further up the chain instead.
nodes.coding_note: The eosinophilic fallback chain is 9965 / 9966 / 9967 → 9964 → 9960 (Pathway §6). 9964 is unavailable here because "do not assign 9964 ... on a normal karyotype" is an explicit alert (Pathway §5.6), so the honest terminal is the next rung, 9960, with karyotype_result_status recording why.

options.label: Pending — record now and re-enter the tool when the result returns
options.upgrade_path: FISH for the CHIC2 deletion or RT-PCR for FIP1L1::PDGFRA would upgrade this to 9965; if negative with clonality shown, to 9964. Result pending — re-enter when it returns.
options.coding_note: Do not treat this as a settled 9960. The FIP1L1::PDGFRA branch is still open, and that diagnosis is imatinib-responsive.

options.label: Not available at this facility — permanent terminal state
options.upgrade_path: FISH (CHIC2) and RT-PCR for FIP1L1::PDGFRA are unavailable; the code cannot be upgraded at this facility.
options.coding_note: Recorded as a permanent unavailable-workup terminal, not as an excluded cryptic set. Consider referral for testing if imatinib is a realistic option.

options.label: Test declined or not done for another reason
options.upgrade_path: FISH (CHIC2) or RT-PCR for FIP1L1::PDGFRA would upgrade this code; the test was not done.

nodes.question: Record the fusion exactly as the report states it.
nodes.capture_label: Genotype as reported (e.g. "ETV6::ABL1 by RT-PCR", "FLT3 fusion, partner not stated")
nodes.hint: The code does not change, but the genotype is preserved on the case record.
nodes.coding_note: ETV6::ABL1 and the FLT3-fusion myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms have no dedicated ICD-O-3.2 code and land provisionally on 9964 (Pathway §5.2). The annotation is always persisted, even though the finding is code-neutral — otherwise the entity is lost permanently.

resolution_logic.coding_note: Provisional landing code. The secondary-cause hard gate and the clonality gate are both satisfied upstream, and the fusion itself demonstrates clonality.
resolution_logic.upgrade_path: None — no ICD-O-3.2 code exists for this entity. The genotype is preserved on the case record instead; revisit if a future ICD-O revision codes it.

nos_fallback.name: Chronic eosinophilic leukemia
nos_fallback.reason: Clonal hypereosinophilia with the secondary causes excluded, but no specific kinase fusion identified.

nodes.question: A clonal karyotype abnormality is shown, but FISH for the CHIC2 deletion or RT-PCR for FIP1L1::PDGFRA was not done. Has it been performed since?
nodes.hint: Clonality is shown, so the case codes 9964 with the missing test named. A positive FIP1L1::PDGFRA result would upgrade it to 9965.
nodes.coding_note: Pathway §3.10 step 5: clonality after secondary causes are excluded gives 9964. The chain 9965 → 9964 → 9960 (§6) reaches 9960 only when clonality is not shown.

options.label: FISH (CHIC2) / RT-PCR now available — go back and enter the result
FISH / RT-PCR requested — result pending
FISH / RT-PCR not available at this facility

nodes.question: Record why FIP1L1::PDGFRA could not be tested. The case codes 9964 with the missing test named.
nodes.hint: 9964, not 9960: clonality is shown by the abnormal karyotype. The missing test is what would move the case up to 9965.
nodes.coding_note: The eosinophilic chain is 9965 / 9966 / 9967 → 9964 → 9960 (Pathway §6). Clonality with secondary causes excluded gives 9964 (§3.10 step 5); the §5.6 bar applies on a normal karyotype only.

options.label: Pending — record now and re-enter the tool when the result returns
options.upgrade_path: FISH for the CHIC2 deletion or RT-PCR for FIP1L1::PDGFRA would upgrade this to 9965 if positive. Result pending — re-enter when it returns.
options.coding_note: Do not treat this as settled. The FIP1L1::PDGFRA branch is still open, and that diagnosis is imatinib-responsive.

options.label: Not available at this facility — permanent terminal state
options.upgrade_path: FISH (CHIC2) and RT-PCR for FIP1L1::PDGFRA are unavailable; the code cannot be upgraded at this facility.
options.coding_note: Do not treat this as settled. The FIP1L1::PDGFRA branch is still open, and that diagnosis is imatinib-responsive.

options.label: Test declined or not done for another reason
options.upgrade_path: FISH (CHIC2) or RT-PCR for FIP1L1::PDGFRA would upgrade this code to 9965 if positive; the test was not done.
options.coding_note: Do not treat this as settled. The FIP1L1::PDGFRA branch is still open, and that diagnosis is imatinib-responsive.

decision_trees.tree_label: Myelodysplastic syndromes, JMML and MDS/MPN overlap

nodes.question: What tests are in this patient's file?
nodes.hint: This is the evidence gate. It fixes what precision is achievable and drives every 'upgrade available' line on the output block.
nodes.coding_note: Group I has no imaging-sufficient route — imaging is staging only (Pathway §0). A case that arrived here from the acute tree's blast gate enters at mds_eb_pediatric_entry or mds_rcc_entry instead and skips this node.

options.label: Referral / clinical note only — no marrow report
Blood film, marrow aspirate or trephine morphology only — no IHC
Marrow aspirate and IHC, no trephine
Trephine and IHC, no marrow aspirate
Marrow aspirate + trephine biopsy with IHC (CD61 / CD41 performed)
options.coding_note: CD61 or CD41 IHC on the trephine is mandatory in paediatric MDS — it identifies the micromegakaryocytes that separate refractory cytopenia of childhood from severe aplastic anaemia (Pathway §3.5).

options.label: Monocytosis-predominant picture — persistent monocytosis with or without splenomegaly (JMML / CMML suspicion)
options.coding_note: JMML is the flagship paediatric Group I MDS/MPN entity. Monocytosis alone is not a diagnosis — reactive monocytosis (TB, HIV, other chronic infection) is the commonest cause in the UCI catchment and must reach a non-reportable terminal (Pathway §3.10, §4.9).

options.label: Hypereosinophilia is the dominant finding, not monocytosis or dysplasia
options.coding_note: The eosinophilia cascade (9964–9968) belongs to the chronic myeloid / MPN tree, not to this one (Pathway §3.10, §7.1). Do not code a clonal eosinophilia terminal from the MDS/JMML tree — exclude parasitic infection and HIV first, then re-enter at the chronic myeloid / MPN tree.

options.label: Malignancy excluded on review — reactive, non-neoplastic or the diagnosis was revised
options.reason: The abstractor recorded that this case is not a reportable malignancy. No morphology code is emitted and the case leaves the malignant registry.

nodes.question: What exactly does the referral or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: A referral naming an entity is not the same as a marrow report establishing it. The wording chooses the NOS parent, never the specific code.
nodes.coding_note: Referral-only tier: confidence is LOW and every downstream test is listed as an upgrade. 9946 and 9985 are never emitted from this node — both require marrow evidence the file does not contain (Pathway §3.4, §3.5).

options.label: Note reads "myelodysplastic syndrome", "MDS", "myelodysplasia" or "preleukaemia" — no marrow report
options.upgrade_path: A marrow aspirate and trephine with CD61/CD41 IHC would separate 9985 (refractory cytopenia of childhood) from 9983 (excess blasts); cytogenetics would add 9986.
options.coding_note: 9989 is the honest referral-tier code. Do not assume 9985 — the commonest paediatric MDS is still a marrow diagnosis.

options.label: Note reads "refractory anaemia", "RAEB", "RARS" or another FAB-era term — no marrow report
options.upgrade_path: A marrow aspirate with a blast count and a trephine would establish the WHO/ICC subtype.
options.coding_note: FAB terms in a referral do not carry a blast count. 9980/9982/9983 all require the marrow report.

options.label: Note reads "JMML", "juvenile myelomonocytic leukaemia" or "juvenile chronic myeloid leukaemia" — no marrow and no molecular report
options.upgrade_path: A marrow report (blasts <20%), BCR::ABL1 exclusion by FISH/RT-PCR and a RAS-pathway panel (PTPN11, KRAS, NRAS, RRAS, NF1, CBL) would establish 9946.
options.coding_note: 9946 requires a somatic RAS-pathway lesion (Pathway §3.4). A referral naming JMML is not that evidence — 9975 is the MDS/MPN NOS parent in the §6 fallback chain (9945 / 9946 → 9975 → 9800).

options.label: Note reads "CMML", "chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia" or "chronic monocytic leukaemia" — no marrow report
options.upgrade_path: A monocyte count (absolute and as % of WBC), a marrow blast count and evidence of dysplasia or clonality would establish 9945.
options.coding_note: CMML needs the two-tier monocyte rule of Pathway §3.10 before 9945 is defensible. 9975 is the NOS parent.

options.label: Note reads "MDS/MPN overlap" or "myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm, unclassifiable"
options.upgrade_path: A marrow report with a blast count, monocyte count and cytogenetics would establish 9945, 9946 or a specific MDS subtype.

options.label: Note reads "therapy-related MDS" / "t-MDS" after prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy
options.upgrade_path: A marrow report would establish the underlying MDS subtype, which is the code; the therapy relationship stays a qualifier.
options.coding_note: DO NOT CODE 9987. Therapy-related MDS is a QUALIFIER on the underlying diagnosis, not a terminal (Pathway §4.8, §5.3.7). 9987 and 9920 are closed as terminals.

options.label: Note reads only "pancytopenia", "bone marrow failure" or "anaemia under investigation" — no malignant diagnosis is asserted
options.reason: The referral asserts a cytopenia, not a malignancy. No morphology code is emitted; the case is not entered on the malignant registry until a marrow report establishes a neoplasm.

nodes.question: What does the marrow aspirate / blood film report describe?
nodes.hint: Iron stain (ring sideroblasts) and cytochemistry count as morphology. A trephine with CD61/CD41 IHC does not — that is the next tier up.
nodes.coding_note: Morphology-only tier. The mandatory paediatric pre-conditions (reversible causes, prior therapy, germline predisposition, IBMFS) are still unasked — every dysplastic option routes into that chain rather than terminating here.

options.label: Cytopenia(s) with dysplasia — marrow blasts under 5%
Cytopenia(s) with dysplasia — marrow blasts 5–19%
Persistent monocytosis with a myeloproliferative picture — circulating myeloid precursors, splenomegaly
Dysplasia described; blast count not stated and no further investigation is possible at this facility
options.upgrade_path: A blast count would separate 9983 from 9985; a trephine with CD61/CD41 IHC would exclude aplastic anaemia; cytogenetics would add 9986.
options.coding_note: A permanent LMIC terminal state, recorded as such. The §5.6 pre-conditions were not documented — germline_predisposition and ibmfs_exclusion_status stay 'not tested' on the output block.

options.label: Marrow reviewed — megaloblastic / reactive change, not dysplasia
options.reason: Marrow morphology showed reactive or megaloblastic change rather than a dysplastic clone. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.

nodes.question: Which pattern does the marrow aspirate and trephine describe?
nodes.hint: Pick the dominant pattern. The blast count is confirmed later, at the gate that actually fixes the code.
nodes.coding_note: Group I has no site resolution — the marrow pattern plus the blast band does the work topography does in solid-tumour groups (Pathway §2.2).

options.descriptor: Monocytosis with myeloproliferative features — splenomegaly, leucocytosis, circulating myeloid precursors
Cytopenia(s) with dysplasia — marrow blasts under 5% and peripheral blasts under 2%
Cytopenia(s) with dysplasia and increased blasts — marrow 5–19%, peripheral 2–19%
options.coding_note: Paediatric MDS with excess blasts is the 5–19% band under ICC. ICC's separate MDS/AML 10–19% category is explicitly excluded under 18 years (Pathway §5.4).

options.descriptor: Ring sideroblasts prominent on the iron stain, with dysplasia
options.coding_note: Ring-sideroblast entities (9982, 9993) are adult-predominant — <1% of paediatric MDS. They stay reachable; the age-implausibility warning travels with them (Pathway §7.5).

options.descriptor: Hypocellular marrow with cytopenias — refractory cytopenia of childhood versus severe aplastic anaemia not yet separated
options.coding_note: About 80% of refractory cytopenia of childhood is hypocellular. CD61/CD41 IHC on the trephine is the discriminator (Pathway §3.5).

options.descriptor: Overlapping myelodysplastic and myeloproliferative features — the CMML, atypical CML and JMML criteria are all unmet
Dysplasia documented but the subtype is not stated in the report
Marrow reviewed — no dysplasia, no excess blasts and no clonal population
options.reason: The marrow shows neither dysplasia nor a clonal population. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.

nodes.question: Absolute peripheral-blood monocyte count?
nodes.hint: Absolute count in ×10⁹/L. The relative criterion (≥10% of WBC) is asked at the next step. Tick 'not documented' rather than guessing — monocytosis is absent in about 7% of true JMML.
nodes.coding_note: ≥1×10⁹/L is the JMML clinical criterion and the CMML one-supporting-criterion tier; 0.5–<1×10⁹/L is the CMML two-supporting-criteria tier (Pathway §3.4, §3.10).

override_when.coding_note: Blasts ≥20% — this is acute leukaemia, not an MDS/MPN. Blasts <20% in both blood and marrow is a MANDATORY JMML criterion (Pathway §3.4); the case belongs in the acute tree.
