bands.coding_note: Meets the JMML monocyte criterion and the CMML ≥1×10⁹/L tier. Reactive monocytosis must be excluded first, especially at this level (Pathway §3.10).
CMML two-tier rule: at 0.5–<1×10⁹/L BOTH supporting criteria are required — dysplasia ≥10% in ≥1 lineage AND clonal cytogenetic/molecular evidence.
Below the monocytosis threshold under both WHO-HAEM5 and ICC — neither CMML nor the JMML monocyte criterion is met. Assess the case as a myelodysplastic syndrome on its marrow pattern instead.
Monocyte count not documented. Monocytosis is absent in about 7% of true JMML, so an undocumented count does not close the JMML branch — it is the genetics that decide (Pathway §3.4).

nos_fallback.name: Myeloproliferative neoplasm, unclassifiable
nos_fallback.reason: MDS/MPN overlap picture recorded but the CMML, aCML and JMML criteria were not met or could not be established.

nodes.question: Is the monocytosis persistent, and have reactive causes been excluded and documented?
nodes.hint: Persistence means ≥3 months unless a clonal marker is already present. In the UCI catchment tuberculosis and HIV are the commonest causes of a persistent monocytosis.
nodes.coding_note: CMUS / CCMUS — persistent monocytosis ≥10% of WBC and ≥0.5×10⁹/L with the CMML criteria unmet — is explicitly not malignant and must not be reported (Pathway §3.10).

options.label: Persistent monocytosis, ≥10% of the white cell count, reactive causes excluded and documented
Reactive cause identified — tuberculosis, HIV, other chronic infection, marrow recovery or G-CSF
options.reason: The monocytosis is reactive (infection, marrow recovery or growth-factor effect). Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).

options.label: Persistent monocytosis but under 10% of the white cell count, or the CMML criteria are otherwise unmet
options.coding_note: The 10% test belongs to CMML. The JMML monocyte criterion is an absolute count of at least 1×10⁹/L with no percentage (Pathway §3.4), so the case still gets the JMML pattern question before it can leave as CMUS (§3.10).

options.label: Splenomegaly and cytopenias fully explained by malaria or HIV hypersplenism
options.reason: Hypersplenism from malaria or HIV accounts for the splenomegaly and cytopenias, and confounds the JMML criteria. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).

options.label: Reactive causes not yet assessed — the file does not document the exclusions
options.coding_note: Recorded as an incomplete exclusion. Reactive monocytosis must be excluded before CMML is coded (Pathway §3.10), so a CMML-pattern answer on this route closes at 9975 with the exclusion named as outstanding.

nodes.question: Which entity does the marrow and clinical picture describe?
nodes.hint: Age is not diagnostic for JMML — it is prognostic only (Pathway §3.4). The genetics decide, not the age.
nodes.coding_note: JMML (9946) and CMML (9945) share a monocytic phenotype and separate on the RAS-pathway lesion and the supporting-criteria rule, not on age.

options.descriptor: Myeloproliferative picture — splenomegaly, elevated HbF for age, circulating myeloid precursors, monosomy 7 (JMML pattern)
Dysplastic monocytic picture — dysplasia ≥10% in ≥1 lineage and/or a clonal marker, no splenomegaly-led myeloproliferative picture (CMML pattern)
Overlapping myelodysplastic and myeloproliferative features — the CMML, atypical CML and JMML criteria are all unmet
Blasts ≥20% in blood or marrow — an acute picture
options.coding_note: Blasts <20% in both blood and marrow is a MANDATORY JMML criterion and bounds CMML too. At ≥20% the case is acute leukaemia and belongs in the acute tree (Pathway §3.4, §3.10).

nodes.question: Two JMML criteria are MANDATORY: blasts under 20% in blood and marrow, and documented absence of BCR::ABL1. What does the file show?
nodes.hint: 'Absence of BCR::ABL1' means a negative FISH or RT-PCR result in the file. A normal karyotype is not that result.
nodes.coding_note: Category I criteria (Pathway §3.4): PB monocytes ≥1×10⁹/L (absent in ~7%), splenomegaly (absent in ~3%), blasts <20% — MANDATORY, absence of BCR::ABL1 — MANDATORY. Only the last two are hard gates.

options.label: BCR::ABL1 excluded — FISH or RT-PCR negative — and blasts under 20% in both blood and marrow
BCR::ABL1 POSITIVE — Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22) on karyotype, or BCR::ABL1 detected by FISH or RT-PCR
options.coding_note: The mandatory JMML criterion fails in the POSITIVE direction, which is diagnostic rather than merely disqualifying. Monocytosis in a Ph-positive case does not make it CMML: the case is owned by the chronic myeloid / MPN tree (Pathway §7.1), which resolves BCR::ABL1-positive disease to 9875 and records the phase as a display-only qualifier. Do not code 9946, 9945 or any MDS terminal here. A positive result codes 9875 whatever else is in the file (Pathway §3.9), so the case goes straight to the phase question instead of through the chronic myeloid evidence checklist, which never read the held answer.

options.label: Blasts under 20% but BCR::ABL1 not tested, or the result is not in the file
options.coding_note: A mandatory criterion is unestablished. 9946 cannot be emitted on this evidence — the case lands on the MDS/MPN NOS parent with the missing tests listed as upgrades (Pathway §3.4, §6 fallback chain).

options.label: Blasts 20% or more in blood or marrow
options.coding_note: The mandatory blast criterion fails. This is acute leukaemia — assign lineage in the acute tree.

options.label: Reviewed — the monocytosis, splenomegaly and cytopenias are fully explained by malaria or HIV hypersplenism
options.reason: Hypersplenism from malaria or HIV accounts for the whole picture and confounds the JMML criteria. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).

nodes.question: Which supporting findings does the file document?
nodes.hint: Supporting criteria are recorded, not decisive. Category II — a RAS-pathway lesion — is what establishes JMML, and it is asked next.
nodes.coding_note: Supporting criteria (Pathway §3.4): HbF elevated for age, circulating myeloid precursors, monosomy 7. None of them changes the code; all of them belong on the output block.

options.label: Splenomegaly present and HbF elevated for age
Splenomegaly present, HbF normal or not tested
No splenomegaly — HbF elevated for age and/or circulating myeloid precursors present
options.coding_note: Splenomegaly is absent in about 3% of true JMML. Its absence does not close the branch.

options.label: Monosomy 7 on cytogenetics, with or without splenomegaly
options.coding_note: Monosomy 7 is supporting, not defining. It is also the commonest cytogenetic abnormality in refractory cytopenia of childhood (~20%) — it does not by itself choose between 9946 and 9985.

options.label: None of the supporting findings is documented

nodes.question: What does the molecular / cytogenetic report show on the RAS pathway?
nodes.hint: Category II requires at least one of these, and it is present in over 95% of true JMML. The distinction that matters is SOMATIC versus germline-only.
nodes.coding_note: DNA-methylation subgroups (low / intermediate / high) are prognostic and code-neutral — all remain 9946. Spontaneous regression (~15%, germline CBL and some NRAS G12S) does not retract the diagnosis: code at diagnosis on the evidence then available (Pathway §3.4, §5.3.9).

options.finding: Somatic PTPN11 mutation (marrow, not germline)
options.coding_note: Somatic PTPN11 is the commonest JMML lesion. Confirm it is somatic — a germline PTPN11 variant alone is Noonan-spectrum myeloproliferation, not JMML.

options.finding: Somatic KRAS mutation
Somatic NRAS mutation
options.coding_note: Some NRAS G12S cases regress spontaneously. Regression is a follow-up fact, not a coding fact — the case stays an incident registration (Pathway §5.3.9).

options.finding: Somatic RRAS mutation
Germline NF1 with loss of heterozygosity, or clinical neurofibromatosis type 1 (≥6 café-au-lait macules over 5 mm)
options.coding_note: Clinical NF1 satisfies Category II without a molecular NF1 report. Record the germline finding as a qualifier on the output block.

options.finding: Germline CBL with loss of heterozygosity
options.coding_note: Germline CBL JMML regresses spontaneously in a substantial minority. It is still an incident case coded at diagnosis (Pathway §5.3.9).

options.finding: Germline PTPN11, KRAS, NRAS or RIT1 ONLY — no somatic secondary lesion, normal karyotype
options.coding_note: Noonan-spectrum myeloproliferative disease. Distinct from JMML and usually self-limiting — do NOT auto-code 9946 (Pathway §3.4, §4.9, §5.6).

options.finding: RAS-pathway panel performed — no lesion identified; an ALK, ROS1, FIP1L1::RARA or CCDC88C::FLT3 fusion, or nothing at all
options.coding_note: ICC-2022's RAS-negative 'JMML-like neoplasm' is NOT adopted (registry decision, Pathway §5.3.2 and §5.4). It has no ICD-O-3.2 code and is coded 9975 on its own merits, with the fusion preserved in genotype_annotation.

options.finding: Monosomy 7 only — no RAS-pathway lesion on a panel that was performed
options.coding_note: Monosomy 7 is supporting, never defining. Without a Category II lesion the case is not JMML.

options.finding: Molecular testing not performed, or unavailable at this facility
options.upgrade_path: A RAS-pathway panel (PTPN11, KRAS, NRAS, RRAS, NF1, CBL, with germline/somatic discrimination) would establish or exclude 9946.
options.coding_note: Category II is unestablished, so 9946 cannot be emitted — the case lands on the MDS/MPN NOS parent (Pathway §6 fallback chain: 9945 / 9946 → 9975 → 9800). "Molecular unavailable at UCI" is a legitimate permanent terminal state, but it must be recorded as such.

nos_fallback.name: Myeloproliferative neoplasm, unclassifiable
nos_fallback.reason: MDS/MPN overlap picture recorded but the CMML, aCML and JMML criteria were not met or could not be established.

nodes.question: Record exactly what molecular or cytogenetic testing the file does contain, and what it showed.
nodes.capture_label: Testing as reported (e.g. "karyotype 46,XY; no FISH, no RAS panel", "no molecular testing performed")
nodes.hint: A mandatory JMML criterion is unestablished. This node records why, so the upgrade line on the output block is accurate.
nodes.coding_note: A JMML with no molecular testing must NOT reach 9946 (Pathway §8 scenario list). 9975 is the honest terminal — the MDS/MPN NOS parent — with the missing tests listed as upgrades.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: BCR::ABL1 by FISH or RT-PCR, and a RAS-pathway panel (PTPN11, KRAS, NRAS, RRAS, NF1, CBL), would establish or exclude 9946.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Absence of BCR::ABL1 is a MANDATORY JMML criterion and it is unestablished here. 9946 is not emitted (Pathway §3.4).

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: A RAS-pathway panel (PTPN11, KRAS, NRAS, RRAS, NF1, CBL) would establish or exclude 9946.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Category II is unestablished. 9975 on its own merits, genotype preserved.

nos_fallback.name: Myeloproliferative neoplasm, unclassifiable
nos_fallback.reason: MDS/MPN overlap picture recorded but the CMML, aCML and JMML criteria were not met or could not be established.

nodes.question: A germline RASopathy variant is present. Has a SOMATIC secondary lesion been documented on the marrow?
nodes.hint: Noonan-spectrum myeloproliferative disease has a germline variant, no somatic second hit, a normal karyotype and a self-limiting course.
nodes.coding_note: This is one of the ten non-reportable mimic points (Pathway §4.9). Forcing an NOS malignant code here would record a cancer that does not exist.

options.label: No somatic secondary lesion; normal karyotype; self-limiting or resolving course — Noonan-spectrum myeloproliferative disease
options.reason: Germline RASopathy (PTPN11, KRAS, NRAS or RIT1) with no somatic secondary lesion, a normal karyotype and a self-limiting course. This is Noonan-spectrum myeloproliferation, not JMML — not a reportable malignancy, no code is emitted (Pathway §3.4, §4.9). Keep under haematology follow-up and re-abstract if a somatic lesion or a clonal cytogenetic abnormality emerges.

options.label: A somatic secondary lesion HAS been documented — a second RAS-pathway hit, monosomy 7 or another clonal marker on the marrow
options.coding_note: Germline RASopathy plus a documented somatic secondary lesion is JMML. The germline variant is recorded as a qualifier, not as the code. ras_pathway_lesion carries the controlled value; record the actual somatic gene or clonal marker verbatim in genotype_annotation, because the controlled vocabulary of Pathway §5.1 has no value for 'somatic secondary lesion, gene unspecified'.

options.label: Somatic testing on the marrow has not been performed — clonality unresolved
options.reason: A germline RASopathy variant with no somatic marrow testing. Clonality is unresolved, so a malignancy is not established: not a reportable malignancy at this point and no code is emitted (Pathway §5.6). Repeat the marrow with somatic RAS-pathway testing and re-abstract if a somatic lesion is found.

nodes.question: Record the fusion or mutation exactly as the report states it.
nodes.capture_label: Genotype as reported (e.g. "CCDC88C::FLT3 by RNA-seq", "ALK fusion by FISH", "monosomy 7 only, RAS panel negative")
nodes.hint: The code does not change, but the genotype is preserved on the case record — otherwise the information is lost permanently.
nodes.coding_note: ICC-2022's 'JMML-like neoplasm' category is NOT adopted (Pathway §5.3.2). RAS-negative JMML phenocopies code 9975 (MDS/MPN, unclassifiable) on their own merits, so 9975 needs no disambiguating note on the code itself.

resolution_logic.coding_note: RAS-negative JMML-like neoplasm recorded as an annotation on 9975.
resolution_logic.upgrade_path: None — no ICD-O-3.2 code exists for this entity. The genotype is preserved on the case record instead.

nos_fallback.name: Myeloproliferative neoplasm, unclassifiable
nos_fallback.reason: MDS/MPN overlap picture recorded but the CMML, aCML and JMML criteria were not met or could not be established.

nodes.question: Which tier of the CMML supporting-criteria rule does this case satisfy?
nodes.hint: Supporting criteria are: dysplasia in ≥10% of cells in ≥1 lineage, and clonal cytogenetic or molecular evidence. How many you need depends on the monocyte count.
nodes.coding_note: CMML-1 (<5% PB / <10% BM blasts) versus CMML-2 (5–19% / 10–19%) is a grade, not a code — both are 9945. WHO-HAEM5 and ICC have converged on the monocyte threshold; there is no divergence to record here (Pathway §5.4).

options.label: Monocytes ≥1×10⁹/L and ≥10% of WBC, blasts under 20%, and AT LEAST ONE supporting criterion — dysplasia ≥10% in ≥1 lineage, OR clonal cytogenetic/molecular evidence
options.coding_note: The one-supporting-criterion tier (Pathway §3.10). Record which criterion was met on the output block.

options.label: Monocytes 0.5–<1×10⁹/L and ≥10% of WBC, blasts under 20%, and BOTH supporting criteria — dysplasia ≥10% in ≥1 lineage AND clonal cytogenetic/molecular evidence
options.coding_note: The two-supporting-criteria tier (Pathway §3.10). Both are required at this monocyte level.

options.label: Blasts in the CMML-2 range (peripheral 5–19% or marrow 10–19%), criteria otherwise met
options.coding_note: CMML-2. The grade is recorded on the output block; the code stays 9945.

options.label: Monocytes 0.5–<1×10⁹/L with only ONE supporting criterion
options.reason: The two-tier CMML rule is not satisfied: at 0.5–<1×10⁹/L both supporting criteria are required. This is CMUS/CCMUS — not malignant, no code is emitted (Pathway §3.10, §4.9).

options.label: Neither supporting criterion has been assessed — no dysplasia assessment and no cytogenetics
options.upgrade_path: A dysplasia assessment on the marrow and cytogenetics/FISH would establish or exclude 9945.
options.coding_note: The monocytic MDS/MPN picture is real but the CMML criteria are unestablished. 9975 is the NOS parent (Pathway §6 fallback chain).

nodes.question: Confirm that the specific MDS/MPN categories have each been considered and excluded.
nodes.hint: 9975 is a diagnosis of exclusion, not a shortcut. It is also the registry's landing code for RAS-negative JMML phenocopies.
nodes.coding_note: 9975 is distinct from 9960 (MPN, NOS, subgroup Ic). The eosinophilia cascade (9964–9968) and atypical CML (9876) belong to the chronic myeloid / MPN tree, not to this one (Pathway §3.10, §7.1).

options.label: CMML, atypical CML, JMML and MDS/MPN-RS-T all considered and excluded — overlapping myelodysplastic and myeloproliferative features remain
options.coding_note: MDS/MPN, unclassifiable, on its own merits.

options.label: Hypereosinophilia dominates and parasitic infection and HIV have BOTH been excluded and documented
options.coding_note: The clonal-eosinophilia terminals (9964–9968) are owned by the chronic myeloid / MPN tree and are never emitted from here (Pathway §3.10, §7.1). This branch now hands the case straight to that tree's hard secondary-cause gate, which re-confirms the parasitic and HIV exclusions — one tap, and no path into 9964–9968 bypasses the gate — and then runs the FIP1L1::PDGFRA / PDGFRB / FGFR1 / PCM1::JAK2 cascade. FIP1L1::PDGFRA is CRYPTIC: a normal karyotype does not exclude 9965 (Pathway §5.6).

options.label: Hypereosinophilia with a secondary cause identified — parasitic infection (strongyloides, schistosoma, filariasis, hookworm, toxocara), HIV, drugs, allergy or autoimmune disease
options.reason: The hypereosinophilia has a documented secondary cause. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted. This is the commonest false-positive registration risk in Group I in the UCI catchment (Pathway §3.10, §4.9).

options.label: Reviewed — the overlap picture is reactive or the diagnosis was revised
options.reason: Reviewed as reactive or non-neoplastic rather than an MDS/MPN overlap neoplasm. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.

nodes.question: Marrow blasts are under 5% and peripheral blasts under 2%. What does the marrow and trephine report support?
nodes.hint: This is refractory cytopenia of childhood territory — the commonest myelodysplastic syndrome of childhood, about 50% of paediatric MDS. Its code is 9985.
nodes.coding_note: Entry point from the acute tree's blast gate (<5% band) and from this tree's own marrow-pattern node. ICC criteria (Pathway §3.5): persistent age-adjusted cytopenia, dysplasia in ≥2 lineages or ≥10% in one, blasts PB <2% / BM <5%, no prior cytotoxic therapy, no fibrosis. About 80% are hypocellular; monosomy 7 in about 20%.

options.label: Persistent age-adjusted cytopenia with dysplasia in ≥2 lineages, or ≥10% dysplasia in a single lineage
Hypocellular marrow with cytopenias — refractory cytopenia of childhood versus severe aplastic anaemia not yet separated
options.coding_note: CD61 or CD41 IHC on the trephine is MANDATORY here — micromegakaryocytes are the feature that separates refractory cytopenia of childhood from severe aplastic anaemia, the key differential (Pathway §3.5).

options.label: Cytopenia only — dysplasia not assessed, no trephine performed
options.coding_note: Without a trephine the aplastic-anaemia differential cannot be closed. Record the omission; it drives the upgrade line.

options.label: Ring sideroblasts prominent on the iron stain
Reviewed — the cytopenia is fully explained by a non-neoplastic cause and there is no dysplastic clone
options.reason: The cytopenia has a documented non-neoplastic cause and no dysplastic clone was found. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).

nodes.question: Which markers does the report list, and what was each result?
nodes.hint: CD61 or CD41 identifies micromegakaryocytes. Their presence is what separates refractory cytopenia of childhood from severe aplastic anaemia.
nodes.coding_note: CD61 / CD41 IHC on the trephine is mandatory in this differential (Pathway §3.5). A negative panel does not by itself code aplastic anaemia — it routes to the aplastic-anaemia and IBMFS exclusions.

marker_groups.group_label: Megakaryocyte panel — mandatory on the trephine

resolution_logic.coding_note: Micromegakaryocytes with 5–19% blasts is paediatric MDS with excess blasts, not refractory cytopenia of childhood.
Micromegakaryocytes present — a dysplastic megakaryocyte lineage. Refractory cytopenia of childhood territory; the mandatory exclusions come next.
CD61-positive micromegakaryocytes are sufficient — CD41 is the alternative, not an additional requirement.
Fibrosis excludes refractory cytopenia of childhood under the ICC criteria (Pathway §3.5). Re-assess the differential before coding.

No micromegakaryocytes in a hypocellular marrow — severe aplastic anaemia and inherited bone-marrow failure are now the leading differentials. No marker combination met. The differential is unresolved and must be settled explicitly — do not default to an MDS code.

nos_fallback.name: Myelodysplastic syndrome, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Myelodysplastic picture recorded but the subtype could not be established.

nodes.question: The marrow is hypocellular without micromegakaryocytes. What does the bone-marrow-failure workup show?
nodes.hint: Chromosome breakage / G2 arrest tests for Fanconi anaemia; telomere length for dyskeratosis congenita and the telomere biology disorders; consider Shwachman-Diamond.
nodes.coding_note: Two of the ten non-reportable mimic points sit here: severe aplastic anaemia and inherited bone-marrow-failure syndromes (Pathway §4.9). Neither may be recorded as an MDS code.

options.label: Hypocellular marrow, no micromegakaryocytes, no dysplasia, normal cytogenetics — severe aplastic anaemia
options.reason: Severe aplastic anaemia — the key differential of refractory cytopenia of childhood. Not a reportable malignancy, no code is emitted (Pathway §3.5, §4.9). Re-abstract if dysplasia, micromegakaryocytes or a clonal cytogenetic abnormality emerge on follow-up.

options.label: Chromosome breakage / G2 arrest abnormal, telomeres short, or a syndromic phenotype — inherited bone-marrow-failure syndrome (Fanconi anaemia, dyskeratosis congenita, Shwachman-Diamond)
options.reason: Inherited bone-marrow-failure syndrome. Not reportable as a myelodysplastic syndrome — no code is emitted; refer to the genetics and haematology services (Pathway §4.9). Re-abstract if the patient later develops MDS or acute leukaemia.

options.label: Dysplasia and/or a clonal cytogenetic abnormality (for example monosomy 7) is present after all
options.coding_note: A clone changes the answer — continue down the myelodysplastic pathway.

options.label: Breakage and telomere testing are not available at this facility — the differential is unresolved
options.reason: Bone-marrow failure with no dysplasia, no micromegakaryocytes and no clonal marker, and with inherited-bone-marrow-failure testing unavailable. A myelodysplastic syndrome is not established, so no code is emitted. Refer for a bone-marrow-failure workup and re-abstract if dysplasia or a clone emerges.

nodes.question: Marrow blasts are 5–19% (peripheral 2–19%). What does the marrow report support?
nodes.hint: Paediatric MDS with excess blasts stays a 5–19% band. ICC's separate MDS/AML 10–19% category does not apply under 18 years.
nodes.coding_note: Entry point from the acute tree's blast gate (5–19% band). Registry arbitration (Pathway §5.4): ICC is used for blast thresholds AND for the <18-years MDS/AML exclusion — a child in the 10–19% band with a dysplastic marrow is paediatric MDS-EB (9983), not MDS/AML.

options.label: Dysplasia documented — continue the mandatory paediatric MDS exclusions (reversible causes, prior therapy, germline predisposition, IBMFS)
Marrow report gives a blast count only — dysplasia not assessed and no trephine performed
options.coding_note: Record the omission. Without a dysplasia assessment the case cannot be separated from a hypoplastic acute leukaemia or from marrow recovery.

options.label: The marrow reads as an acute picture rather than dysplasia — sheets of blasts, no maturation
options.coding_note: Return to the acute tree and assign lineage. A missed AML/APL is the costlier error (Pathway §7.1).

options.label: No dysplasia — the blast increase and cytopenia are explained by a recovering marrow, B12/folate deficiency or infection
options.reason: The blast increase is reactive — marrow recovery, nutritional deficiency or infection — with no dysplastic clone. Not a reportable malignancy, no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).

nodes.question: Have the reversible causes of cytopenia and dysplasia-like change been excluded and documented?
nodes.hint: Uganda addition to the ICC criteria: exclude nutritional (B12, folate, iron) and HIV-related cytopenia and macrocytosis BEFORE any paediatric MDS code.
nodes.coding_note: This gate does not change the code; it decides whether there is a code at all. Its result is carried on the output block.

options.label: B12 / folate / iron deficiency, HIV, chronic infection and drug effect all excluded and documented
Nutritional deficiency (B12, folate or iron) identified and the cytopenia or macrocytosis is attributable to it
options.reason: Nutritional deficiency accounts for the macrocytosis and dysplasia-like change. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §3.5, §4.9). Re-abstract if the picture persists after replacement.

options.label: HIV-related cytopenia or HIV-associated marrow change accounts for the picture
options.reason: HIV-related marrow change accounts for the cytopenia and dysplasia-like features. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §3.5, §4.9).

options.label: Malaria or HIV hypersplenism accounts for the splenomegaly and cytopenias
options.reason: Hypersplenism from malaria or HIV accounts for the splenomegaly and cytopenias. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).

options.label: Not assessed — the file does not document these exclusions
options.coding_note: The case can still be coded, but the omission is recorded and appears as a workup row on the output block. Skipping this step is the largest single false-positive registration risk in this group.

nodes.question: What germline predisposition and inherited-bone-marrow-failure testing does the file document?
nodes.hint: About 20% of refractory cytopenia of childhood has an underlying germline hit, so this is high-yield. It does not change the code — it must be recorded.
nodes.coding_note: Mandatory pre-condition before any sporadic paediatric MDS code (Pathway §3.5): a germline predisposition screen (GATA2, SAMD9/SAMD9L, RUNX1, ANKRD26, ETV6) and an IBMFS exclusion (chromosome breakage / G2 arrest, telomere length; consider Shwachman-Diamond). Recorded as a modifier on the output block.

options.label: Germline panel performed — no predisposition variant; breakage and telomere testing normal
Germline GATA2 variant identified
options.coding_note: GATA2 deficiency is the commonest germline predisposition in paediatric MDS with monosomy 7. It is a modifier, not a code — the MDS subtype still sets the code.

options.label: Germline SAMD9 or SAMD9L variant identified
options.coding_note: SAMD9/SAMD9L (MIRAGE, ataxia-pancytopenia) is associated with monosomy 7 and with somatic reversion. Modifier only.

options.label: Germline RUNX1, ETV6 or ANKRD26 variant identified
options.coding_note: Familial platelet disorder with predisposition to myeloid malignancy. Modifier only — the code is still the MDS subtype.

options.label: Chromosome breakage / G2 arrest abnormal, or telomeres short — inherited bone-marrow-failure syndrome
options.reason: Inherited bone-marrow-failure syndrome (Fanconi anaemia, dyskeratosis congenita or a related telomere biology disorder). Not reportable as a myelodysplastic syndrome — no code is emitted; refer to genetics and haematology (Pathway §3.5, §4.9). Re-abstract if the patient later develops MDS or acute leukaemia.

options.label: Germline and IBMFS testing are not available at this facility
options.coding_note: The code is unchanged, but the omission MUST be recorded — it appears as a workup row and an upgrade line on the output block (Pathway §5.6).

nodes.question: Which cytogenetic / FISH finding does the report give?
nodes.hint: Cytogenetics in paediatric MDS are prognostic and supporting; only isolated del(5q) is code-defining, and it is confirmed with the blast count and the dysplasia pattern.
nodes.coding_note: Monosomy 7 is the commonest abnormality in paediatric MDS (~20% of refractory cytopenia of childhood) and is NOT code-defining. SEER over-counting rule (Pathway §3.5): within the MDS family code only the first subtype diagnosed — do not re-abstract a later, more specific subtype.

options.finding: Monosomy 7 or del(7q)
options.coding_note: Supporting, not defining. It appears in refractory cytopenia of childhood, in paediatric MDS-EB, in GATA2 deficiency and in JMML alike.

options.finding: Isolated del(5q)
options.coding_note: 9986 requires the deletion to be ISOLATED and the blast count to be under 5%. Both are confirmed at the next two steps before the code is emitted.

options.finding: Complex karyotype — three or more abnormalities
options.coding_note: Prognostically adverse, not code-defining within the MDS family.

options.finding: Trisomy 8, del(20q), or another single abnormality
Karyotype normal
options.coding_note: A normal karyotype does not exclude a myelodysplastic syndrome — the diagnosis rests on persistent cytopenia plus dysplasia, not on a clone.

options.finding: An AML-defining abnormality — PML::RARA, RUNX1::RUNX1T1, CBFB::MYH11, KMT2A-r, NUP98-r or MECOM-r
options.coding_note: This is not a myelodysplastic syndrome. Under WHO-HAEM5 a defining abnormality makes the case AML at any blast percentage; ICC applies a ≥10% floor to the same list. Either way the case leaves this tree for the acute tree.

options.finding: Cytogenetics not performed, or unavailable at this facility
options.coding_note: "Cytogenetics unavailable at UCI" is a legitimate, permanent terminal state — but it must be recorded as such, not passed off as a completed workup. 9986 is not reachable without it.

nos_fallback.name: Myelodysplastic syndrome, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Myelodysplastic picture recorded but the subtype could not be established.

nodes.question: Marrow blast percentage (of ALL nucleated marrow cells)?
nodes.hint: The denominator is all nucleated cells, not non-erythroid cells. If the acute tree already recorded a blast count, re-enter the same value — this is the gate that fixes the code. Tick 'not documented' rather than guessing.
nodes.coding_note: The blast band is what separates 9983 from the low-blast MDS codes. The all-nucleated-cell denominator retires the old erythroid/myeloid split (Pathway §2.2).

override_when.coding_note: A defining AML abnormality overrides the blast threshold under WHO-HAEM5; ICC applies a ≥10% floor to the same list. Either way this is not a myelodysplastic syndrome.

bands.coding_note: ≥20% is acute leukaemia under both WHO-HAEM5 and ICC — no divergence. Leave the MDS tree and assign lineage.

ICC's MDS/AML 10–19% category is explicitly EXCLUDED under 18 years (Pathway §5.4). In a child a dysplastic marrow at 10–19% blasts is paediatric MDS with excess blasts — 9983 — not MDS/AML. In an adult patient this band would be MDS/AML under ICC; flag for review if the patient is 18 or over.
bands.upgrade_path: None on the blast count. Cytogenetics/FISH would add prognostic detail; the code is unchanged.

bands.coding_note: Paediatric MDS with excess blasts: BM 5–19%, PB 2–19% (Pathway §3.5). The 5–19% band is retained for children under both the ICC arbitration and the registry's code list.
bands.upgrade_path: None on the blast count. Cytogenetics/FISH would add prognostic detail; the code is unchanged.

bands.coding_note: BM <5% / PB <2% — low-blast territory. The dysplasia pattern now chooses between 9985, 9980, 9982, 9993, 9986 and 9989.
Blast percentage undocumented. A band entered earlier is kept (Pathway §2.2, §6): the next screen asks which band the report gave, so a 5–19% report is not turned into a low-blast code.

nos_fallback.name: Myelodysplastic syndrome, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Myelodysplastic picture recorded but the subtype could not be established.

nodes.question: Which dysplasia pattern does the marrow and trephine report describe?
nodes.hint: Blasts are under 5% in the marrow and under 2% in the blood. The dysplasia pattern now chooses the code.
nodes.coding_note: 9985 is THE paediatric refractory-cytopenia-of-childhood code and the commonest myelodysplastic syndrome of childhood, about 50% (Pathway §3.5). SEER lists 'refractory cytopenia of childhood' and 'childhood MDS with low blasts' as explicit alternate names for 9985/3.

options.descriptor: Dysplasia in ≥2 lineages, or ≥10% dysplasia in a single lineage, with persistent age-adjusted cytopenia — refractory cytopenia of childhood
options.coding_note: Refractory cytopenia of childhood / childhood MDS with low blasts. About 80% are hypocellular with patchy erythroid islands; monosomy 7 in about 20%. CD61/CD41 IHC must have separated this from severe aplastic anaemia.
options.upgrade_path: None on the code. Germline predisposition and IBMFS results, if still outstanding, are recorded as modifiers.

options.descriptor: Single-lineage dysplasia, anaemia predominant, no ring sideroblasts
options.coding_note: 9980 (refractory anaemia) is a FAB-era term retained for the single-lineage presentation; the retired codes 9991 (refractory neutropenia) and 9992 (refractory thrombocytopenia) alias to it. In a child, review whether the multilineage criteria are in fact met — 9985 is the commoner paediatric assignment.
options.upgrade_path: A repeat trephine assessing all three lineages would establish whether the case is in fact 9985.

options.descriptor: Ring sideroblasts ≥15% (or ≥5% with SF3B1), single-lineage dysplasia
options.coding_note: Under 1% of paediatric myelodysplastic syndromes. Kept reachable for the genuine rare paediatric case, with the age-implausibility warning attached (Pathway §7.5).

options.descriptor: Ring sideroblasts with MULTILINEAGE dysplasia, with or without SF3B1
options.coding_note: 9993 was ADDED in ICD-O-3.2 (Pathway §5.7). Adult-predominant; kept reachable with the age-implausibility warning.

options.descriptor: Dysplasia documented but the subtype is not stated, or the lineages involved are not recorded
options.coding_note: 9989 is the MDS fallback when the subtype is undocumented. It is a real terminal, not a placeholder — but the missing detail is listed as an upgrade.
options.upgrade_path: A trephine reporting dysplasia by lineage would establish 9985 or 9980; an iron stain would establish 9982 or 9993; cytogenetics would establish 9986.

options.descriptor: Reviewed — no dysplasia; the cytopenia is non-neoplastic
options.reason: No dysplastic clone on review — the cytopenia is non-neoplastic. Not a reportable malignancy, no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).

nodes.question: Which entity does the marrow and clinical picture describe?
nodes.hint: Age is not diagnostic for JMML — it is prognostic only (Pathway §3.4). The genetics decide, not the age.
nodes.coding_note: JMML (9946) and CMML (9945) share a monocytic phenotype and separate on the RAS-pathway lesion and the supporting-criteria rule, not on age.

options.descriptor: Myeloproliferative picture — splenomegaly, elevated HbF for age, circulating myeloid precursors, monosomy 7 (JMML pattern)
Dysplastic monocytic picture — dysplasia ≥10% in ≥1 lineage and/or a clonal marker, no splenomegaly-led myeloproliferative picture (CMML pattern)
Overlapping myelodysplastic and myeloproliferative features — the CMML, atypical CML and JMML criteria are all unmet
Blasts ≥20% in blood or marrow — an acute picture
options.coding_note: Blasts <20% in both blood and marrow is a MANDATORY JMML criterion and bounds CMML too. At ≥20% the case is acute leukaemia and belongs in the acute tree (Pathway §3.4, §3.10).

nodes.question: Reactive causes of the monocytosis were not excluded and documented, so the CMML criteria cannot be confirmed. What does the file support?
nodes.hint: CMML needs reactive monocytosis excluded first (Pathway §3.10).
nodes.coding_note: Pathway §3.10: exclude reactive monocytosis before CMML (9945). With the exclusion undocumented the criteria are not established and the chain 9945 → 9975 (§6) steps down. Ruling 11 of 4 Sep 2026: an untested result drops to the nearest code.

options.label: Monocytosis with dysplasia and/or a clonal marker; reactive causes still to be excluded
options.upgrade_path: Documentation that reactive causes are excluded would allow 9945 if the CMML supporting criteria are met.

options.label: Reviewed — the monocytosis is reactive
options.reason: Reactive monocytosis is not a neoplasm and is not reported (Pathway §3.10, §4.9).

nodes.question: CMML is excluded on the percentage or criteria. Does the picture fit JMML?
nodes.hint: Age is not diagnostic for JMML. The genetics decide, not the age (Pathway §3.4).
nodes.coding_note: The JMML monocyte criterion has no percentage test (Pathway §3.4). Monocytosis that fits neither JMML nor CMML is CMUS or CCMUS: not malignant, no code (§3.10, §4.9).

options.descriptor: Myeloproliferative picture — splenomegaly, elevated HbF for age, circulating myeloid precursors, monosomy 7 (JMML pattern)
No JMML pattern — monocytosis of undetermined significance (CMUS / CCMUS)
options.reason: Clonal or idiopathic monocytosis of undetermined significance (CMUS/CCMUS). Explicitly not malignant and must not be reported (Pathway §3.10, §4.9).

ICC's MDS/AML 10–19% category is explicitly EXCLUDED under 18 years (Pathway §5.4). In a child a dysplastic marrow at 10–19% blasts is paediatric MDS with excess blasts — 9983 — not MDS/AML. In an adult patient this band would be MDS/AML under ICC; flag for review if the patient is 18 or over.
bands.upgrade_path: None on the blast count. Cytogenetics/FISH would add prognostic detail; the code is unchanged.
